caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 304 of 2004
lawyer:
M.A. Azim, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Firoz Shah, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
For Respondents ----- Not represented.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works, Bangladesh Secretariat, Dhaka ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The First Court of Settlement, Bangladesh Abandoned Building, Segunbagicha, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 8th November, 2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 5789 of 2003)
full_judgment:
This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated November 8, 2003 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court in Writ Petition No. 5789 of 2003 summarily rejecting the Writ Petition on the following finding:

"Since the matter has been finally decided by the superior Court as regards the title and possession there is no good ground for challenging the judgment and order of the Court of Settlement. Besides, there is great latches on the part of the petitioner as the Writ petition has been filed beyond time by 11 years."

The Writ Petition was filed against the judgment dated November 22, 1992 of the 1st Court of Settlement in case No. 762/88 (Ka-3-Block-F, Joint Quarter, Mohammadpur, Dhaka House No. 1/9 Block-F, Joint Quarter, Mohammadpur, Dhaka (Ka-25).

2. It was the case of the petitioners before the Court of Settlement that Abdur Razzaque who was the owner of the property sold the same to the petitioner (before the Court of Settlement) in 1964 and sine then they were in possession through tenant but latter of some of tenants upon manipulation managed to have the property declared as abandoned property. The petitioners' father Azizur Rahman was a voter and he died in Bangladesh on 14.8.77 That the petitioners applied to the authority for release of the property from the list of abandoned property, but without any success.

3. The Petition filed before the Court of Settlement by Respondent Nos. 2-3 herein was opposed by the Government, without filing any written objection, denying the assertions of the aforesaid respondents. It was submitted from the side of the Government that the petitioners (before the Court of Settlement) filed Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 and obtained decree declaring title of the petitioners and that the property is not an abandon property and that appeal against the decree in the aforesaid suit was without any success and that the decree in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 has been maintained by the Appellate Division.

4. The Court of Settlement allowed the case upon observing-

"As the question of abandonment of the house was involved in the above Title suit. No. 671 of 1985 filed prior to the publication of the notice declaring the case house as abandoned property, it is evident that the list was prepared in contravention of proviso (b) of article 5 of the Ordinance No. 54".

5. The Court of settlement upon allowing the case directed the authority to exclude the property from 'Ka' list of the abandoned property. The Court of Settlement while allowing the case observed "the title in the case building shall abide by the decision made in the Civil Court: It may be mentioned that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 was challenged in title Appeal No. 179 of 1988 of the Court of Sub-Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka and the same was dismissed. There upon the Government move the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 95 of 1992 and the Rule obtained was discharged Government there upon filed Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 807 of 1997 and the same was dismissed. It was observed by this Court while dismissing the Civil Petition for leave to appeal "it appears that on consideration of the evidence on record the High Court Division found that the Court below Concurrently held that the plaintiffs are the real owners of the suit property and they were very much present in Bangladesh during the war of liberation and afterwards. The genuineness of exhibit-1 and 2 have not been challenged or questioned before the Trial Court or even before the appellate Court and no such ground has also been taken in the revisional application. The Courts below also concurrently found that the plaintiffs were in possession of the suit property and they are also all through in control and management and supervision of the same till the Government illegally took over the property at the behest of D.W. 2 We have heard at length of the learned Deputy Attorney General who failed to point out any legal infirmity in the Judgment of the High Court Division. Consequently we are of the view that there is nothing to interfere with the same."

6. It may be mentioned that Exhib-1 was the lease deed of Abdur Razzaque and Exhib-2 was the sale deed dated January 3, 1964 on the basis of which plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 claimed the property in suit it is seen from the judgment of this Court in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 807 of 1997 that the original documents were produced before the trial Court before he appellate Court and also before the Court of Settlement and thereafter the documents were lost and for that photo copy was filed before the High Court Division.

7. The Respondent Nos. 2-3 in the light of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 filed the case before the Court of Settlement seeking release of the property from the list of abandon property. The case so filed by the respondent Nos. 2-3 before the Court of Settlement was contested by the Government and in presence of the learned lawyer of the Government the Court of Settlement allowed the case with direction to the authority to release the property from the list of abandoned property. As mentioned herein before the Court of Settlement made its judgment on November 22, 1992. The Government obtained certified copy of the judgment on the court of Settlement on 27.12.92 (vide paragraph-11 of the Writ Petition No. 5788 of 2003). The Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 804 of 2004 has been filed against the judgment in Writ Petition No. 5789 of 2003. As it is seen from the order passed in Civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 807 of 1997 that title of the respondent Nos. 2-3 has been settle by the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 which was affirmed by the appellate Court, thereafter by the High Court Division and finally by this Court. In the said suit it was also declared that the property in question was not abandon property.

8. As against the judgment of the Court of Settlement, the Government move the High Court Division by fling writ petition No. 5789 of 2003 which was affirmed on September 25, 2003 and was moved before the High Court Division any time thereafter. The affidavit in the writ petition was affirmed after lapse of 10 years 10 months and 3 days. The petitioner Government tried to explain the said delay stating that after obtaining the certified copy of the judgment of the court of settlement on 27.12.1992, "the matter was placed before the writ committee" and the said committee after making decision sent file to the Ministry of Works and the said Ministry's law cell sent the file to the Solicitor wing (writ) and the said Wing of the Solicitor sent the record to the Office of the Attorney general on 2.2.2002 to file writ petition and that in the office of the Attorney General the file was misplaced and remained untraced for long time and thus there was delay of 10 years 10 months. It has been stated in paragraph-11 of the Writ petition "the delay is bona fide without any willful negligence of the petitioner and as such it is submitted that the delay may be condoned in the interest of justice".

9. The High Court Division summarily rejected the writ petition on the ground that the title of the property in question of the Respondent Nos. 2-3 and possession thereof of the claimants (Respondent Nos. 2-3) as well as the question of the property being not abandoned property have been settled in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 an also by the judgment and order of the Court of Settlement an that the petition was out of time for about 11 years. The explanation offered for the condonation of delay has been made upon making statement in lump. Under the law writ petition was required to be filed upon explaining each day's delay but that was not done. The Writ petitioner tried to offer explanation of delay making lump statement. We do no find that the High Court Division committed any error is not considering the statement made seeking condone of delay as reasonable and sufficient.

<u>10. We are of the view the High Court Division was quite correct in refusing to interfere the Judgment of the Court of Settlement as in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 title of the respondent Nos. 2-3 was found in the property in question and also considering he materials on record it was held that the property was not an abandon property. As mentioned herein before the Judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 was upheld by the court of appeal and thereafter by the High Court Division and finally by this Court. The High Court Division did not interfere with the judgment of the Court of Settlement also for not explaining the delay satisfactorily. The matter of condonation of delay in the facts and circumstance of a particular case and also in the background of explaining the delay satisfactorily is the discretionary power/jurisdiction of the Court, in the instant case is of the High Court Division. Unless the exercise of discretionary power is arbitrary or not logical this court does not interfere with the order of the High Court Division rejecting prayer for condonation of delay. In an exceptional case which is rare of the rarest, tough order of the High Court Division in the matter of condonation of delay was free from infirmity as mentioned above, still has interfered with the order of High Court Division, in exercise of this court's power to prevent gross failure of justice or that one of the parties in the proceeding has obtained unjust advantage or benefit because of latched of the persons who conducted the case for the Government or person who instructed the learned lawyer of the Government in the prosecution of the proceeding, but the instant case is not of the kind because of the facts stated above.</u>

11. At the recent time it is seen that Civil Petition for leave to Appeal Civil appeal and civil Revision by the Government is filed after inordinate delay and attempt is being made to explain the inordinate delay making statement that the file travels different tables in connection with making decision for moving the High Court Division and the Appellate Division and thus there has been delay. The statement made seeking condonation of inordinate delay is of lump nature and that some time statement made in seeking condonation of delay is either casual or of the fashion or kind as stated herein before. It is also seen that attempt is made to explain the delay, as in the instant case, by making statement that relevant file was misplaced, mixed up with some other records or became untraceable and at one time the file was found or that recently the file was found and the petition is filed and thus the delay so occurred was unintentional. We have noticed in the instant case the Government tried to explain the delay in filing Writ Petition by making lump statement. Making of lump statement while offering explanation as to reason of delay has always been deprecated and also has been considered not satisfactory explanation since settle law is that delay of each day shall have be explained satisfactory.

<u>12. The statement made in paragraph-11 of the writ petition No. 5789 of 2003 which was filed challenging legality of the judgment of the 1st Court of Settlement dated 22.11.92 shows the state of play in the office of Attorney general, office of the Solicitor and in different Ministries which is of recent origin. In our view time is high for coming out of the state of play in filing case after inordinate delay upon making statement for condonation of delay which is nothing but got up story to shield latches, negligence and also cases of purposely making the case time barred. The Government, except in a case of highly exceptional nature, cannot have preferential treatment in the matter of condonation of limitation juxtaposition to the ordinary litigant and that the Government cannot have preferential treatment on the question of limitation in bulk number of case's, as is being noticed by us, since law of limitation equally applies to the Government as well as to the ordinary litigant. The present Civil Petition for leave to Appeal has been filed taking ground that Government machineries move slowly and as such time is consumed in taking decision and thus in the matter of delay while prayer for condonation is made by Government the same needs lenient consideration. The ground so taken merits not consideration since the explanation offered was found not sufficient and the delay was not sufficiently explained as was required by law. The other ground i.e. ground No. 2 is of no merit since the question as to whether the property was an abandon property or not was set at rest by the decree of title Suit No. 671 of 1985 and same having been maintained by this Court.</u>

13. It may be mentioned that the complexion of Title Suit No. 106 of 1984 and Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 was quite different and Judgment and decree is title Suit No. 106 of 1984 has no relevancy to the subject matter of Title Suit No. 671 of 1985. It has been held in Title Suit No. 671 of 1985 that the plaintiffs at all material time were in Bangladesh and that they are the owners of the property in question and they were in management and control of the property in question and that they also were in supervision of the property till rently Government illegally took over the property at the behest D.W. 2.

<u>14. In the afore state of the matter We do not find any ground to interfere with the judgment of the High Court Division sought to be appealed.</u>

Accordingly, the Leave Petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 333 of 2008
lawyer:
Kamal-ul-Alam, Advocate instructed by Md. Toufiq Hossain, Advocate-on-Record.   ------ For the Petitioners 
Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For Respondent No.2
Respondent No.1 ------ Not represented.
parties:
M/S M.M. Steel & Limited and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
The Judge, First Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong and another ------ Respondents.
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 21.08.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.7258 of 2007.)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: Instant leave petition under Article 103 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 21.08.2007 passed in Writ Petition No. 7258 of 2007 by the High Court Division summarily rejecting the petition.

<u>2. The Writ Petition No.7258 of 2007 was filed challenging the order No. 12 dated 26.06.2007 passed in Artha Rin Execution Case No.08 of 2007 by the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, rejecting the writ petitioner's application filed under Sections 28 and 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissing the Execution Case on the ground of limitation.</u>

<u>3. The Islami Bank Limited as plaintiff filed Artha Rin Suit No. 02 of 2005 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong, against the defendant for recovery of Tk. 39,71,334/- contending, amongst others, that the defendant, though enjoyed the loan facilities from the bank, failed to repay the same within time or thereafter, inspite of repeated demands made for repayment. The suit was decreed for Tk. 39,71,334/- with cost fixing Tk.43,297/-, payable in four equal installments with interest @ 8% p.a. and in case of default of payment of any installment the decree could be satisfied through execution case. As the defendant judgment- debtor failed to make repayment of any installment the decree holder bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No.8 of 2007 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat-1, Chittagong. The judgment debtor entered appearance and on 09.05.2007 filed an application under Sections 28 and 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissing the Execution Case asserting to be barred by limitation and that the application was heard on 26.06.2007. The executing Court on hearing the contesting parties rejected the application observing, amongst others, that the judgment debtors submitted that in terms of the decree the first installment was to be paid within three months from the date of the decree and as the judgment debtors failed to make the payment within the said period, the execution case, as per Section 28 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, required to be filed within 180 days from the expiry of the last day of the period allowed for payment of the first installment and as per Section 29 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the period is to be counted from the last day of the period allowed for making payment of the defaulted installment, as allowed by the Court, and that in the instant case, the suit was decreed on 26.07.2005 and as such the first installment was due within three months thereafter i.e. within 25.10.2005. But the execution case has been filed on 24.01,2007 i.e. after about 474 days. Therefore the execution as filed is exfacie time barred. The Decree holder resisted the application contending, amongst others, that the learned Court ordered for payment of the decreetal amount in 4 equal installments within one year without specifying the dates for payment of the installments and the judgment debtor was allowed to make the payment of the decreetal amount in four installments within the period of One year and as such the installments could he paid even within the last four months of the year or last four days of the year. The court did not specify the period or time frame on which the installments were to be paid. There is no order for making payment of quarterly equal installments as claimed by the judgment debtor-petitioners. The Executing Court accepted the submissions of the decree holder and accordingly rejected the application. However the Executing Court allowed time for payment of the decreetal amount within 20.02.2007. Being aggrieved the judgment debtors filed the Writ Petition No.7258 of 2007 challenging the aforesaid order of rejection in the High Court Division and that the Rule issued therein was heard and disposed of by the impugned judgment and order dated 21.08.2007. On behalf of the writ  petitioner it was submitted that the decree in question was passed on 26.07.2005 ordering payment of the decreetal amount in four equal installments within one year and that the judgment debtor petitioners failed to pay any of the installments and as such the period for payment of the first installment expired with the expiry of three months from the date of passing of the decree, hence the period of limitation for filing execution case started to run from the expiry date of such three months from the date of decree, and that the execution case ought to have been filed within six months after the expiry of said three months from the date of the decree add thereby the execution case ought to have been filed within nine months from the date of the decree i.e. within 25.04.2006, whereas the execution case was filed on 24.01.2007 and thus the execution case as filed was barred by limitation and hence the execution case is liable to be dismissed.</u>

<u>4. The High Court Division on consideration of the submissions made by the learned advocate as well as the materials on record, the provisions of law, the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat and the impugned order passed by the executing Court rejected the writ petition summarily, observing that: "We have considered that submission of the learned Advocate and gone through the impugned order and other relevant papers annexed to the writ petition. We have examined the decree in question (Annexure-A). The relevant portion of this decree reads thus: “বিবাদীগনকে ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা রায় প্রকাশের এক বছরের মধ্যে সমান ৪ কিস্তিতে বার্ষিক ৮ ভাগ মুনাফা মতে বাদী ব্যাংক বরাবরে পরিশোধ করার নির্শেশ প্রদান করা হলো। বিবাদীগন কোন একটি কিস্তি প্রদানে ব্যর্থ হলে বাদী ব্যাংক আইনানুগভাবে বিবাদীগনের নিকট থেকে ডিক্রিকৃত টাকা বার্ষিক ৮ ভাগ মুনাফাসহ মোকদ্দমা দায়েরের তারিখ থেকে আদায়কাল পর্যন্ত আদায় করে পাওয়ার অধিকারী হবেন” From this decree it is very much clear that the Artha Rin Adalat, though I allowed the writ petitioner to pay the decreetal amount in 4 equal installments within total period of 1 year but did not mention any time limit for payment of any of these installments within that one year time . So, obviously the petitioner could have deposited the 1st installment and also any other installment at any time within that one year. So obviously the limitation for filing the execution case started to run from the darn of expiry of this one year time. So, we find that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat has rightly rejected the petitioner's prayer for dismissal of the execution case on the ground of limitation.</u>

5. We have perused the leave petition as well as the impugned order. We have also perused the order passed by the executing Court and the contents of the decree, which are annexed to the leave petition. We have also considered the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner to the effect that the High Court Division was wrong in not holding that a literal interpretation of the provision for payment of decreetal amount within year in four equal installments, as provided in Section 49 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, would mean payment of the decreetal amount in four quarterly equal installments in one year, otherwise the provision of Section 28, 29 and 49(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 will became meaningless and that the High Court Division was not justified in holding that the decree as passed in the suit directing payment of the decreetal amount in four equal installments within one year without mentioning any time-frame as to the mode of payment of the installments and thus holding that the period of limitation for filing execution case will commence from the date of expiry of one year is not proper. The teamed Advocate however admitted that in the decree there is no mention of any specific date or period on which the installments were to be paid. Since in the decree no specific date has been mentioned for payment of the installments and the judgment debtor were allowed to make the payment of the decreetal amount in installments, which is in fact a facility given to the judgment debtor to make the payment of the decreetal amount in part, instead of making the payment of the decreetal amount at a time, and there being no mention of specific dates for payment of the installments the judgment debtors were allowed to make the payment of the decreetal amount within one year in four installments and thus the mode of payment of installments was made flexible. In the premises, in the instant case, we are of the view that the reasons given by the High Court Division, quoted above, are in accordance with law and therefore no interference is called for.

6. Accordingly, the application for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2119 of 2008
lawyer:
Dr. M. Zahir, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record  ------ For the Petitioner 
Md. Abdur Nur, Advocate-on-Record   ------ For Respondent No.3 
Respondent Nos. 1-2 ------ Not represented
parties:
K.M. Muzahid Islam ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs of Bangladeshi. Secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka-1000 and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 04.12 2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1426 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: Instant leave petition under Article 103 of the Constitution is for granting leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 04.12.2007 passed in Writ Petition No.1426 of 2006 by a Division Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule.

<u>2. The petitioner hereof filed the Writ Petition No.1426 of 2006 challenging the Order No.11 dated 05.42006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka, in Artha Rin Execution Case No.490 of 2005 rejecting the petitioner's application filed under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for dismissal of the Execution Case.</u>

3. Facts relevant in the instant case are that the respondent No.3 bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.56 of 2004 in the Artha Rin Adalat, 2nd Court, Dhaka, on 20.04.2004 praying for recovery of money and for foreclosure of mortgage property stating that the petitioner as Managing Director of M/S. A1-Faruque  Textile Mills Limited availed a loan facility of Tk. 4,39,31,000/- for setting up of a 'textile Mills, against which both movable and immovable property of said company were mortgaged to the bank as security and apart from that the said Managing Director and other Directors of the Borrower Company also stood guarantors for the repayment of the loan within the stipulated time, for which several agreements were executed in between the bank and the borrower company as well as the Managing Director and Directors of the Borrower Company.

<u>4. The respondent bank sanctioned Tk. 4,18,50,000/-out of which the borrower company availed TK. 4,39,31,000/-  and the loan amount was disbursed in between 30.12.1986 and 20.01.1991 and that the Textile Mills Unit went into operation in August, 1988. It was stipulated that the foreign currency loan amount out of the total loan amount was to be paid hack in 15 half-yearly installments effective from 30.06.1988 and the local currency loan amount was to be repaid in 18 half-yearly installments effective from 31.12.1989 with interest as agreed upon. The borrower company and its Directors failed to make the repayment as per stipulated installments and as such a legal notice dated 19.11.1991 was sent under Section-34 of the Bangladesh Shilpa Bank Order and on receipt of the said notice the borrower Company and the guarantors prayed for reschedule repayment of the repayment schedule of the loan, to which the bank after discussions agreed, on certain specific conditions, to which the borrower company and its Directors agreed and confirmed the acceptance of the conditions by their letter dated 15.11.1998 but for reasons best known to them, they did not execute the formal document, and then by a letter dated 30.12.1998 they prayed for moratorium of one year for payment of the down payment as per the rescheduled repayment scheme, mentioned hereinbefore, to which the respondent bank by its letter dated 09.03.1999 asked the borrower company and its Directors to comply with the agreed rescheduled repayment scheme within 15 days in default to initiate legal proceeding against them for realization of the outstanding loan amount but the said borrower Company prayed for further facilities in the form of waiver of the accrued interest and others, and the Board of Directors of the bank in its meeting held on 01.08.2000 considered the prayer of the Borrower Company and allowed certain financial benefit and rescheduled the repayment schedule of the loan but the Borrower Company again defaulted and that a cheque issued by it was bounced and in such circumstances the respondent bank took steps for auction sale of the mortgaged property through publication auction notice in dailies "Inquilab" and "Bangladesh Observer" but there was no proper response and that the respondent bank's subsequent efforts to auction sale of the property failed because of filing of Writ Petition No. 5133 of 2003 in the High Court Division by the Borrower Company challenging the notice of the auction sale, and that ultimately Rule was discharged and then the Borrower Company moved the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal unsuccessfully. Faced with such situation the respondent bank filed the Artha Rin Suit for recovery of Tk. 44,12,56,166/-, which includes the principal amount and the interest amount accrued thereon. The suit was decreed exparte vide judgment and decree dated 08.11.2004 and pursuant to said decree the respondent-bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No. 49 of 2005 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka, on 22.03.2005, for satisfaction of the decree and in the said Execution Case, the petitioner hereof on 05.02.2006 filed application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 praying for dismissal of the execution case on the ground that the claim of the respondent bank as made is violative of the provision of Section-47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and that the decree as passed has violated the provision of Section-12 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and thus the decree is a nullity, which was heard and disposed of by the impugned order dated 05.02.2006 rejecting the said application, observing that:</u>

<u>“অত্রাদালতের অভিমত এই যে, অত্রাদালত বর্তমানে একটি জারী আদালত এবং আত্রাদালতকে শুধুমাত্র ডিক্রীকেই অনানয়ন করিতে হইবে। মূল মামলায় কিভাবে ডিক্রী হইয়াছে তাহা জারী মামলায় দ্রষ্টব্যের নহে। দায়ীকে বিবাদীপক্ষে ঐ ডিক্রীকে অবৈধ বলিতে চাহিলে তাহা রদ রহিতের জন্য বিধি মোতাবেক অগ্রসর হইতে হইবে। এইরূপ অর্থঋণ আদালত আইন-২০০৩ এর ৫৭ ধারায় একটি দরখাস্ত প্রদান করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার পাইবে না। সুতরাং ৩নং দায়িকের অত্র দরখাস্ত নামঞ্জুর করা গেল।”</u>

<u>5. The High Court Division on detailed discussion as to the provision of Section-47, the date on which the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force and the provisions of Sections-5(3) and (4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and on consideration of the materials on record and the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties discharged the Rule, observing that:-</u>

<u>"According to sub-section (3) of section 5 of Artha Rin Adalat, 2003 only the decree for foreclosure requires to be made final and according to sub-section (4) of section 5 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 other decrees passed by the Artha Rin Adalat become final with the sale of mortgaged property. The Sub-section (4) of section 5 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 makes it clear that save and except the decrees passed in mortgage suits for foreclosure the decrees passed in other mortgage suits also do not require to be made final for the purpose of starting of the execution case. In the present case though in the plaint a decree for foreclosure was prayed for but the Artha Rin Adalat passed a simple money decree only. So we do not accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the writ petitioner that the impugned decree require to be made final before stating of the execution case and as such the execution case in question started on the basis of preliminary decree cannot continue further.</u>

<u>In the writ petition though the validity of section 47(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 has been challenged but at the time of hearing of the rule no question was against before us from the side of the writ petitioner as to the validity of this section. The learned Advocate for the writ petitioner, of course has argued that the impugned decree was passed violating the provision of this section. The learned Advocate has argued that according to this section 47 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 the lending bank can not claim any amount exceeding 200% of the loan amount advanced by it to the petitioner and the Adalat also passed the decree for that claimed amount violating the provision of this section 47. The learned Advocate has contended that this decree passed in contravention of section 47 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is illegal and void and as such it can not be executed. But we do not accept this argument of the learned Advocate for the writ petitioner. Section 47 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into operation on 1st May, 2004 and the suit in question was filed 20th April, 2004. The provision of section 47 was not all applicable in this suit."</u>

6. Being aggrieved the leave petitioner has come up with the instant application. The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner submitted that the High Court Division has erred in not considering that, the decree as passed Is had, since the suit has been filed with a claim containing the interest amount, which is more than 300% of the principal loan amount and thus violated the provision of Section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, hereinafter referring to as the Ain, and that the High Court Division have failed to appreciate that the decree has been passed ignoring the provision of Section 12(6) of the Ain, which bars filing of suit without adjustment the sale proceeds of mortgaged property. The learned Advocate in elaborating his submission on Section 47(3) of the Ain stated that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain came into force on  On March, 2003 and accordingly Section-47 came into force on 10th April, 2004 whereas the case was filed on 20.04.2004 i.e. within limitation but the Court below illegally held that the borrower company is not entitled to get the benefit under Section 47(3) which runs as under:

“৪৭(৩) এই ধারায় বিধানটি এই আইন বলবৎ হইবার এক বছর পর কার্যকর হইবেঃ তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান, ইচ্ছা করিলে, এই ধারা কার্যকর হইবার পূর্বেই, এই ধারার বিধান অনুসরণ করিতে পারিবে”

7. Admittedly the suit has been filed adding interest amount more than 300% inasmuch as the principal amount of the loan enjoyed was 4,39,31,000/- and the suit has been filed claiming Tk.44,12,56,166/- with further interest @ 14.5% effective from 01.07.2002. The learned Advocate submitted that as per Section-5 of the General Clauses Act any Act or law, in which the date of commencement is not specifically mentioned, such Act or law conies into force on the day it is published in the official gazette and that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 was published in the official gazette on 10.03.2003 and the Section 1(3) mentions that all other Sections, other than the Sections-46 and 47, shall come into force with effect from 01.05.2003 and the Section-47 will come into force one year after 'the Ain' comes into force and that even if word 'বলবৎ' as appearing in Section 47(3) Mv the Anm and the word 'কার্যকর' as appearing in Sections 1(3) and 47(3) of the Ain has the same meaning there is distinction in the meanings of the words `Act' and `Section'. Act is defined in Article 152 of the Constitution but the words ধারা or বিধান have not been defined. The learned Advocate submitted that Section 1(3) of the Ain cannot be said to mean that `the Ain' itself came into force with effect from 01.05.2003, since it has been clearly mentioned therein that all the Sections of the Ain except Sections-46 and 47 will come into force with effect from 01.05.2003, whereas the Ain has been promulgated on 10.03.2003 and therefore `the Ain' has become 'বলবৎ' for the purpose of Section-47(3) on 10.03.2003 and that even if the word ধারা and বিধান are given the same meaning but those are not synonymous to the word and therefore the word আইন mentioned in Section 47(3) means Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, itself, which became বলবৎ, on 10.03.2003 with its publication in the Gazette and therefore Section 47 became effective i.e. কার্যকর one year thereafter i.e. on 10.03.2004 and accordingly the borrower company is entitled to get the benefit of Section 47 in the calculation of the claimable interest amount and that the suit amount containing the interest amount as added being not in conformity with the provision of Section 47 of the Ain, the decree for the amount as passed is illegal. Consequently the execution case as filed for realization of the decreed amount is not maintainable and hence the impugned judgment and order passed by their lordships in the writ petition discharging the Rule is liable to be set aside.

8. We have perused the leave petition as well as the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in discharging the Rule and the order passed by the Executing Court rejecting the application filed under Section 57 of the Ain. It appears that the learned Advocate has made his submission on the basis of Sections-5(2) and (3) of the Ain and did not take into consideration the provision of Section, 5(4) of the Ain in its true perspective. In order to appreciate the aforesaid provisions of law we are quoting those herein below:

৫। আদালতের একক এখতিয়ার। (১) অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৫) ও (৬) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের ঋণ আদায় সম্পর্কিত যাবতীয় মামলা ধারা ৪ এর অধীন প্রতিষ্ঠিত, ঘোষিত বা গণ্য হওয়া অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে দায়ের করিতে হইবে এবং উক্ত আদালতেই উহাদের নিষ্পত্তি হইবে।

(২) এই আইনের অধীন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান, স্থাবর সম্পত্তি জামানত স্বরূপ বন্ধক গ্রহণপূর্বক প্রদত্ত ঋণের বিপরীতে উক্ত বন্ধকী স্থাবর সম্পত্তির বিক্রয় (Sale) বা নিষ্ক্রিয় সম্পত্তির ((Foreclosure)  উদ্দেশ্যে The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (Act No. IV of 1882) এর Section 67 অধীন এবং the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act No. V of 1908) এর Order XXXIV বিধান অনুযায়ী কোন বন্ধকী মামলা ((Mortgage suit) দায়ের করিতে চাহিলে, উক্ত মামলাও এই আইনের অধীন প্রতিষ্ঠিত অর্থ ঋণ আদালতেই দায়ের করিতে হইবে; এবং এইরূপ ক্ষেত্রে Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 এর বিধান সমূহ এই আইনের বিধানসমূহের সহিত, যতদূর সম্ভব, সমন্বয়ের মাধ্যমে প্রযোজ্য হইবে।

৩। উপ-ধারা (২) এই অধীন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত মামলা নিষ্ক্রিয় সমাপ্তির (Foreclosure) উদ্দেশ্যে একটি বন্ধকী মামলা (Mortgage suit) হইলে, কেবলমাত্র সেই ক্ষেত্রে আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী (Preliminary decree) হইবে এবং অন্যান্য সকল ক্ষেত্রে ঋণ আদায়র্থ দায়েরকৃত মামলায় আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রী চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রী (Final decree) হইবে।

৪) The Transfer of Property Act, 1882 অথবা বর্তমানে প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইনের বিপরীতে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, উপ-ধারা (৩) এর অধীনে বন্ধকী মামলা ব্যতিরেকে, এই আইনের অধীন দায়েরকৃত কোন মামলায়, আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ডিক্রি বাদী আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানের পক্ষে নিষ্ক্রিয় সমপ্তি (Foreclosure) প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে, এবং ঋণের বিপরীতে বাদীর অনুকূলে বন্ধকী স্থাবর সম্পত্তি ডিক্রির ধারাবাহিকতায় নিলাম বিক্রয় হওয়া মাত্রই উক্ত প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রী হিসাবে গণ্য হইবে, এবং বিক্রয় চুড়ান্ত ও ক্রয় বৈধ গণ্য হইবে এবং অতঃপর উক্ত সম্পত্তি পুনরুদ্ধার করিবার কোনরূপ অধিকার (Right to  redeem) বিবাদী-দায়িকের থাকিবে না।

9. Further to appreciate aforesaid provisions having regard to the facts and circumstances of the instant case we need to look into the prayer portion of the plaint as filed in the Artha Rin Suit No.56 of 2004, which is as under:

“অতএব বাদীপক্ষে বিনীত প্রার্থনা এই যে,

(ক) বাদীপক্ষের অনুকূলে এবং বিবাদীগণের প্রতিকূলে ৩০/০৬/২০০২ ইং তারিখের হিসাব অনুযায়ী ৪৪, ১২,৫৬,১৬৬/- টাকা এবং ০১/০৭/২০০২ ইং তারিখ হইতে চূড়ান্ত দিন পর্যন্ত ১৪.৫% হারে সুদসহ টাকা আদায়ের ব্যক্তিগত ডিক্রীসহ প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী দিতে;

(খ) প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী মোতাবেক বিবাদীগণ ডিক্রীকৃত অর্থ পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে নিষ্ক্রীয় সম্পত্তির আদেশসহ বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি বিক্রয়ের মাধ্যমে বাদী সংস্থার পাওনা আদায়ের চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রী দিতে;

(গ) মামলার খরচ বাদীর অনুকূলে এবং বিবাদীগণের বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রী দিতে।

(ঘ) বাদী আইনানুযায়ী আর যে যে প্রতিকার পাইতে হকদার তাহার ডিক্রী দিতে মাননীয় আদালতের মর্জি হয়।

10. It appears from the prayer portion, quoted above, that the respondent-bank has prayed for a personal decree in preliminary form and further prayed for sale of the mortgaged property in case of default on the part of the judgment debtor in satisfying the decree, to be passed. Thus the suit as framed and filed can not be said to attract Section 5(3) of the Ain but the same attracts Section 5(4) of the Ain and therefore a decree passed in preliminary form after sale of the mortgage property automatically The becomes a final decree. Thus we do not find any substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate that the decree, being passed in preliminary form, cannot be put into execution for realization of decreetal amount by sale of the mortgage property, before Making the decree final, and hence the decree is bad in the eye of law.

11. The submission of the learned Advocate as to filing of the suit without complying with Section 12(6) of the AM is bad in the eye of law inasmuch as the amount claimed in the suit has not been fixed in accordance with the provision of said Sub-Section 6. Section 12(3) provides that without taking step for sale of the mortgage property no suit can be filed but averment has been made in the plaint of the suit that the Bank has taken steps for auction sale of the mortgaged at least on: two occasions, which attempts failed at the instance of the judgment debtors. It appears that the respondent-bank took steps for auction sale of the mortgage national property by publication of the auction notice in the national dailies and the judgment-debtors by filing writ petition stopped the sale of the mortgaged property through auction and thus the suit as franc i and filed is In accordance with law.

12. The learned Advocate has given much stress on the provisions of Section 47 and Section 1(3) of the Ain. Section 1(3) provides that:

“এই আইনের ধারা ৪৬ ও ৪৭ এর বিধানদ্বয় উক্ত ধারাদ্বয়ে উল্লিখিত সময়ে এবং বাকী বিদানসমূহ ২০০৩ সালের ১লা মে তারিখ হইতে কার্যকর হইবে।

and Section 47 provides that:-

“৪৭। দাবী আরোপে সীমাবদ্ধতা-(১) বর্তমানে প্রচলিত অন্য কোন আইন বা পক্ষগনের মধ্যে সম্পাদিত সংশ্লিষ্ট চুক্তিতে যাহাই থাকুক না কেন, এই আইনের অধীন মামলা দায়েরের ক্ষেত্রে, কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান কোন ঋন গ্রহীতাকে প্রদত্ত আসল ঋনের উপর দায় এমনভাবে আরোপ করিয়া আদালতে মামলা দায়ের করিবে না, যাহাতে আদালতে উত্থাপিত উক্ত সমুদয় দাবী আসল ঋন অপেক্ষা ২০০%(১০০+১০০)=৩০০ টাকা) এর আর্থিক হয়।

(২) উপ-ধারা(১) এর বর্ণিত মতে আসল ঋন অপেক্ষা ২০০% এর অধিক অনুরুপ দাবী আদালত কর্তৃক গ্রহনযোগ্য হইবে না।

(৩) এই ধারার বিধানটি এই আইন বলবৎ হইবার এক বৎসর পর কার্যকর হইবেঃ তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, কোন আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান, ই্ছা করিলে, এই ধারা কার্যকর হইবার পূর্বেই, এই ধারার বিধান অনুসরন করিতে পারিবে।”

<u>13. In Section 1(3) the word “কার্যকর” has been specifically Mentioned and it contains that except Sections 46 and 47, all other Sections of 'the Ain' were to become effective from 1st May, 2003 and that Section 47(3) provides vides that the said Section-47 is to come into force one year after the said 'Ain' comes into force. In the said Section-47(3) the words বলবৎ“ and কার্যকর appear. The word “কার্যকর” means to become effective i.e. coming into force. The word বলবৎ“ as per dictionary meaning (Samsad's Bengali to English Dictionary published by Sahitta Samsad, Calcutta, India) in English, is 'operative', in force' and the word 'বলবৎ' means in English language is to put into force. We required the learned Advocate to provide us with the meaning of the word .বলবৎ“ in English language and also to place before us any material showing the English Meaning of the word “বলবৎ“but he submitted that he could not find the same. Thus we take English meaning of the word “বলবৎ“as 'operative' or 'coming into force' as per the aforementioned Dictionary. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain has been promulgated (জারী হইয়াছে) on 10.03.2003 and by Section 1(3) the said Ain was made effective “কার্যকর/বলবৎ" from May, 2003 except it's Sections 46 and 47, Which were made effective from the dates mentioned in the respective sections. Section 47 provides that the said section would come into force one year after the 'Ain' becomes effective or comes into force. The Artha Rin Adalat Ain consists of 60 sections and out of those 60 sections, 58 sections came into force with effect from 01.05.2003 as mentioned in Section-1(3) and the rest two sections i.e. Sections 46 and 47 came into force on the dates mentioned in the respective sections. The date 10.03.2003 is the date of promulgation (জারী হওয়া) of the law and the date mentioned in Section 1(3) of the Ain are the dates on which the said law came in-to force or became effective. In the premises we are of the view that Section 47 became effective one year after the date on which the Artha Rin Adalat Ain came into force, which is on 01.05.2003, and thus the provisions of Section 47 came into force with effect from 1st May, 2004. Hence the suit in reference filed on 20.04.2004, the leave petitioner and for that matter the borrower company and or its Director are not entitled to get benefit of Section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. Thus we do not find any merit in the leave petition.</u>

14. Accordingly, the application for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J:- This civil review petition is directed against the judgment and order dated 30.07.2008 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 697 of 2007 dismissing the same. 

2. The respondent No.1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 62 of 1988 for declaration of his title in .21 acres of land in plot No. 243 and .17 acres in plot No. 254 of Mouza Gobindapur, Police Station and District-. Jhenaidah and for recovery of possession of .04 acre of land of plot No.243 and entire .17 acre of land of plot No. 254. 

3. In the said suit the plaintiff stated, inter-alia, that .21 acres of land of plot No. 243 belong to Nayeb Ali and others and they transferred the same to Abdur Rahim Sheikh by a deed of Sale dated 08.02.39 and after his death his son Mahatab Sheikh got the same and he settled the same in favour of Hemat Ali, thereafter the plaintiff on the 14th Chaitra, 1346 B.S.; that .17 acres of land in plot No. 254 was settled to Abdur Rahim Sheikh by aforesaid Nayab Ali on 04.08.38 and Tezarat and Alekjan on 08.02.39 by patta. After death of said Rahim Sheikh his son Mahatab got the same and by a registered Kabuliyat dated 28.5.48 he settled the same in favour of father of the petitioner; that the father of the plaintiff orally gifted the said .21 acre of land of plot No. 243 and the same was recorded in the name of the petitioner; that the father of the petitioner transferred .17 acres of land of plot No. 254 in favour of the petitioner by a sale deed dated 23.1.1997; that for the first time on 15th magh, 1383 B.S. the petitioner could know that .17 acre of land of plot No. 254 was wrongly recorded in the name of Rajah Ali and Makshed All and against the said wrong recording the petitioner filed Title suit No. 256 of 1973 and the same was decreed exparte; that regarding .21 acre of land of plot No. 243, Title Suit No. 690 of 1976 was filed. During pendency of the said suit there was a compromise and it was decided that the petitioner will possess "Kha" schedule land and the said Rahela will possess "Ka" schedule land but no deed of exchange was executed; that in the mean-time the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff from "Kha" schedule land on 25.03.86; that thereafter defendant No. 5 dispossessed the plaintiff, subsequently there was a shalish and the defendant handed over .17 acres from "Ka" schedule of land to the plaintiff and he is living with his family on the said land and since defendants are denying the title of the plaintiff in the suit land he is compelled to file the instant suit. 

4. The petitioner as defendant No. 1 con-tested the suit by filing written statement stating, interalia, that Rahim Sheikh, being owner in the land of both the schedules died leaving behind only son Mahtab Sheikh and he orally settled the same to Barkatullah Mollah in 1346 B.S. and subsequently on his demand executed and registered a Kabuliyat dated 07.06.1948 and the aforesaid landlord accepted the said Kabuliyat and granted Dakhila accepting him as a tenant; that subsequently said Barkatullah transferred his instrest in the said land to Yousuf Ali Biswas by executing a registered patta dated 16.07.1952; that Yousuf Ali Biswas being owner and possessor of the said land transferred to Rajab Ali Kazi and Makscd Ali Kazi by registered sale deed dated 19 Kartik 1362 13.S. thereafter they transferred the same to Hasina Khatun by a registered deed of sale dated 03.10.1973; that said Hasina Khatun transferred the same to Rahela Khatun by a registered deed of sale dated 27.02.1976 and she was possessing the same through defendant No.1 who is her bargadar; that Rahela Khatun entered an agreement to transfer the said land to Elahi Mondal, defendant No. 1 and one Lutfor Rahman who was her relation: that since said Rahela Khatun did not execute deed of transfer, within time the defendant and said Lutfar Rahman filed a suit for specific performance of contract and obtained sale deed from Court on 23.05.1990 by filing a suit for specific performance of contact; that subsequently the defendant entered into an agreement to transfer the suit land to Mojibur Rahman and on acceptance of Taka 24,000/- handed over possession of the suit land and said Mojibur Rahman is a bonafide purchaser of the suit land for value and before Mojibur Rahman the defendant possessed the suit land for more that 12 years; that already a Miscellaneous Case has been filed to set aside the decree obtained by the petitioner against Rahela and this circumstances the instant suit filed by the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed. 

5. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Jhenaidah by the judgment and decree dated 20.08.1999 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant-petitioner preferred Title Appeal No. 125 of 1999 which was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 30.06.2000 Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant preferred Civil Revision No. 3380 of 2000 before the High Court Division who by the judgment and order dated 25.01.2007 dis-charged the Rule affirming the concurrent finding of facts passed by the courts below observing that there is no reason to interfere with the judgment and decree passed by the court of appeal below as there is no illegality in the said Judgment and order. 

6. Thereafter the petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid Judgment and order filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 697 of 2007 before this Division Which was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 30.07.2008. The petitioner being aggrieved by the afore-said judgment and order dated 30.07.2008 preferred the instant Civil Review Petition before the Appellate Division. 

7. We have heard Mr. N.K. Saha, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner, and Mr. Nawab Ali, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the respondent No.1 and perused the impugned judgment of this Division and also perused the other judgments in question and also other materials available on record. It appears that in the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal this Division considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner to the effect that- the trial court decreed the suit holding that the plaintiff claimed his title on the basis of deed of settlement dated 28.05.1948 which was registered prior to the registered kabuliyat dated 07.06.1948 produced by the defendant and further the title of the plaintiff has already been declared in Title Suit No. 265 of 1976 and though the defendant claimed the Title Suit No. 295 of 1996 challenging the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 265 of 1976 yet he did not get any relief therein and further the evidence on record also show that the plaintiff was given possession in kha schedule land but thereafter the plaintiff was dispossessed from a portion thereof. 

8. The Appellate Division in dismissing the leave petition rightly observed as follows:-
"It appears that the High Court Division on a meticulous examination of the judgment of the trial court as well as lower appellate Court and also considering evidence on record held that the lower appellate Court after discussing the evidence both oral and documentary, elaborately and after proper assessment of evidence on record came to the finding that the plaintiff had been able to prove his right title and possession in the suit land and further the concurrent finding of facts should not be disturbed unless it is manifestly perverse and some are of the view that there being no illegality or infirmity in the above decision no interference is called for." 

9. Having considered all the aspect of the matter we are of the view that this Division earlier in dismissing the leave petition took into consideration all relevant materials on record and arrived on a correct decision and as such we do not find any new ground for review of the impugned Judgment and Order. 

10. Accordingly, this review petition is dismissed. 

End.

Mohammad Fazlul Karim J.:- This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 12th day of May, 2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 195 of 1999 allowing the appeal decreeing the Title Suit No. 4 of 1997. 

2. The facts involved in the. case, in short, are that the suit land originally belonged to Zamindars Babu Sunil Chandra Ghose, Kiron Chandra Ghose and others and while in khas possession through 3 pattans in 1351, 1352 and 1353 B.S. they gave the land under settlement to sheikh Wahab Ali after 'receiving  salami and issuing proper dakhilas and said Wahab Ali erected dwelling house over plot No. 784 and used to live there with family and in other plots used to cultivate and grow different crops and in this way S.A. and R.S. record were prepared in the name of Wahab Ali; that in the said records his name entered wrongly with the names of superior Zaminders; that Wahab Ali died leaving son Siddiqur Rahman, widow Sajan Bibi and daughter Sahatan who inherited the property and subsequently, the widow and daughter gifted their shares in favour of Siddiqur Rahman through registered instrument and delivered possession; that on 30.03.1985 corresponding to 16th Chaitra 1391 B.S.. Md. Siddiqur Rahman exchanged the property by registered instrument with the plaintiff and through that deed the plaintiff became owner and possessor of the scheduled land; that in the first part of Falgun, 1387 B.S. the defendant No. 1 tried to dispossess the plaintiff on the plea of leave taken by him as vested and non-resident property and said Md. Siddiqur Rahman and others file Title Suit No. 106 of 1981 before the Court of Munsif, Manikganj which subsequently, renumbered as Title Suit No. 215 of 1984 and on 30.06.1987 the decree was passed declaring the title of Md. Siddiqur Rahman and plaintiff and also declaring that the suit land is not vested and non-resident   property.

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the materials facts contending, inter-alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Ex7land-lords Kiron Chandra and others and he along with his brothers would barga cultivate the suit land under the landlords and afterwards said landlords proposed to sell the suit land the defendant No. 2 agreed to purchase the same and accordingly, they executed 2(two) bainanamas in favour of the defendant No. 2 on 31.12.1962 and delivered the possession of the suit land in favour of the defendant No. 2, but the deed of transfer could not be registered due to imposition of restrictions on the transfer for land of the Hindu Citizens; that Ex-landlord Shashi Bhusan Saha and others who left for India during the Indo-Pak war in 1965 and accordingly, it was enlisted as the enemy property and thereafter, as vested and non-resident property and that the suit land has been lease out to the defendant No. 2 vide VP Case No. 1 /Satu/81/ who has been possessing the same paying lease money to the Government and that all the papers of the plaintiff are false and as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

4. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the trial Court on consideration of evidence on record dismissed the suit in holding that after abolition of Zamindary system the suit property was lying abandoned and taking that advantage both the plaintiff and contesting defendants are trying their best for garbing the suit property with all vague and fraudulent papers; that the plaintiff claimed title by way of registered deed of. exchange dated 30.03.1985 with one Md. Siddiqur Rahman who claimed himself as the son of Sheik Wahab All and from the pleading of the plaintiff the plaint and the oral evidence of P.W.'s same contradictions appears regarding acquisitions of title of Sheikh Wahab AIi by way of pattan from superior Zamindar the High Court Division in absence of proof of chain of title of the plaintiffs predecessor declared title of the plaintiff on the llagis of judgment of earlier suit being Title Suit No. 215 of 1984 filed by Md. Siddiqur Rahman and Title Suit No. 106 of 1981 in the Court of the then 1st Munsif Court, Manikganj which was before the registered deed of exchange dated 30.03.1985; that the plaintiffs predecessor got 3 pattans in 1351, 1352 and .1353 B.S. corresponding to 1944 A.D., 1945 A.D. and 1946 A.D. which was considered by the trial Court as exhitit-1, 1(a) and 1(b) of earlier Title Suit No.215 of 1984 in which the S.A. Khatian numbers were inserted although S.A. operation started after the abolition of zamindary system and finally published in 1962 A.D. the High Court Division over-looked that in a document of 1944, 1945 and 1946 A.D. the number came in the year 1962 inserted upon fraudulent Act and thus, committed error of law in decreeing the suit. The learned Counsel further submitted that upon fraudulent document no declaration of title cannot be declared by a competent Court, the High Court Division erred in law in decreeing the suit without formal proof of exhibit-6 shows 1st party's name Siddiqur Rahman who belonged 'Ka' scheduled property comprising plot Nos. 595, 455, 674 and 707 but exhibit Nos.Kha(7), Kha(4) and Kha(10) show that Nurul Islam was not owner in plot Nos. 155, 455, 495, 707 and 674 and thus plaintiff Nurul Islam was not owner of 16 annas share in 'Kha' schedule property of exhibit No. 6 and thus the deed of exchange was executed by giving upon vague schedule of land and the plaintiff did not acquire title over 'Ka' schedule of property of exhibit-6; that the trial Court found the pattans in the name of Sheikh Wahab Ali a forged,- fraudulent antedated and further no possession was delivered vide exhibit No. 6, the High Court Division nowhere discussed those material evidence but decreed the suit in holding that the plaintiffs title has been declared in earlier suit in which Md. Siddiqur Rahman was plaintiff and thus, the judgment is liable to be set aside. 

5. It appears that the trial Court, the Court of Appeal below and the High Court Division found the plaintiffs title and possession in the suit land. The plaintiff has been able to prove his title in the suit land. The plaintiff has also been able to prove that the defendant dispossessed him from the suit land in the last part of Shraban, 1395.B.S. It further appears that the Court below found that the plaintiff was able to prove the alleged fact of dispossession as narrated in the plaint. The witnesses of the plaintiff have also proved the alleged fact of dispossession as narrated in the plaint. The plaintiff has also been able to prove his title to the suit land by adducing reliable oral and documentary evidence. It also appears that the statements of the defendants are contradictory and as such, not acceptable in the eye of law. 

6. In view of the above, we find no substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners. 

7. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed. 

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel  Hossain J. This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and decree dated 10.03.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.2889 of 2003 making the Rule absolute and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 21.05.2003 (decree signed on 28.05.2003) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Chittagong in Other Appeal No.04 of 2003 affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.09.2002 (decree signed on 06.10.2002) in Other Suit No.08 of 1999 decreeing the suit.

2. The petitioners as plaintiffs filed a suit being Other Suit No.8 of 1999 in the Court of 1st Joint District Judge, Chittagong for declaration of title by way of inheritance and adverse possession impleading the respondent Nos.1-3 as defendants.

3. The plaint case, in short, is that the suit land along with other land was under the Nayabad Taluk of Azmat Ali Khan which was taken settlement by Golam Gafur Sawdagar and Azgar Ali by registered deed dated 20.02.1877. The earlier suit land was used as a tea garden and that subsequently the Government gave possession of some portion of the land in favour of the settlement receiver Golam Gafur Sawdagar and thereafter Government took possession of the remaining land and handed over the same to the Chittagong District Council (Chittagong Zilla Parishad); that the said, Golam Gafur being dead was inherited by his 4 sons Kala Miah, Asmat Ali, Abdus samad and Abdul Gani and 2 daughters Ammajan and Misreijan as the legal heirs of Golam Gafur and that Golam Gafur Sawdagar being died before C.S. operation the propperty of said Golam Gafur was recorded in the name of his son Kala Miah under C.S. Khatian No. 130 being dag No. 338 as the other sons and daughters of Golam Gafur Sawdagar were minor at that time and the C.S. recorded Kala Miah died before marriage   and as such the land recorded in C.S. Khatian being amicably partitioned was lonely obtained by Abdul Gani brother of Kala Miah and that the said Abdul Gani being dead before R.S. operation and the suit land was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 982 in the name of Noor Husain, son of said Abdul Gani; that the R.S. recorded tenant Noor Hossain sold out the entire R.S. recorded property of R.S. Dag No. 931 and 932 by a Registered kabala being No 222 dated 26.01.1994 claiming possession to have been transferred to Mokbul Ahamed and that the said property by a Registered Kabala No. 1744 dated 19.05.1948 was transferred to Haji Fazar Rahman and sale Ahamed sawdagar with its possession and the Sale Ahmed, Sawdagar sold his portion of the suit land by 2 registered deed being No. 3487 dated 02.10.1950 and 3488 dated 02.10.1950: and by another registered deed No. 3644 dated 12.10.1950 to Abdul Monaf Contractor including the possession of the land in question and that in the P.S. Settlement the suit land was recorded as P.S. Khatian No. 1208 and 1214 and the property in question was recorded their 8, annas share in the name of Haji Fazar Rahman and the rest 8 annas share in the name of Abdul Monaf Contractor and that the P.S. recorded owner Abdul Monaf Contractor being in possession of the suit land of the 8 annas property as mentioned above constructed pucca and semi pucca structures and developed the land in question by spending huge amount and that suit property within the pourashava the holding was recorded in the name of the predecessor of plaintiff, petitioner Abul Monaf Contractor and the same was rented out by him and that the holding tax of the Municipality was regularly paid by the plaintiffs petitioner in continuation of their predecessor and that the B.S. record of suit land was recorded in the name of Abdul Monaf Contractor as per his right and possession and that the B.S. record holder Abdul Monaf Contractor being dead the suit land was inherited by his legal heirs the present petitioners and respondent Nos. 5 and 6 and by way of continuing the payments of rents and tax as before being in continued possession and as such the right of possession was established. That it is further case of the plaintiffs that due to the introduction of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the right of the defendant-respondent No.1 the appellant petitioner the Villa parishad having been abolished and the rent receiving interest of Zilla Parishad do not exist and the plaintiffs-petitioners in continuation with their earlier ownership are in possession with their recorded right in the suit land through their predecessor-in-interest Noor Hossain in whose name the suit land was recorded in R.S. Khatian No. 982 and that R.S. Khatian No. 981 was recorded in the name of defendant-respondent No.1 the Zilla Parishad. That though the defendant respondent-Zilla Parishad's right to realise rent from the plaintiff was extinguished it served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act upon the plaintiffs-petitioners which created cloud over their right, title and interest in the suit land and that the plaintiffs-petitioners failed to get relief in Other Class Suit No. 95 of 1992 as they sought irrelevant relief in the said suit and that some of the tenants of the plaintiffs-petitioners in collusion with the staffs of the defendant- respondent No. 1 denied the right and title of the plaintiffs for which the plaintiffs-petitioners were compelled to institute the suit against the defendants-respondents.

4. That the defendant-respondent No.1 Zilla Parishad contested the suit by filing written statement stating, inter-alia, that by the registered settlement dated 20.02.1977 the predecessor of the plaintiffs Golam Gafur Sawdagar did not acquire any right, title and possession and there is no continuation of the same by the plaintiffs-petitioners and that the suit land as per R.S. Khatian No. 982 is not possible to be ascertained without local investigation and that the names of the predecessors of the plaintiffs-petitioners in R.S. P.S and B.S Khatian were wrongly recorded having no legal basis and that the disputed land of R.S. Khatian No. 982 along with the land of R.S. Khatian No. 981 was entirely vested with the defendant-respondent No. 1 being the property of the Bharat Samrat without any rent and that taking the advantage of carelessness of the staffs of Zilla Parishad R.S. Khatian No.982 was wrongly recorded in the name of Noor Hossain as occupant of the suit land and that the suit land was never given settlement in the name of R.S. recorded (occupant Noor Hosain and no rent was collected from him being the settlement holder or the land in question and that the wrongly recorded P.S. and B.S. Khatian being in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs-petitioners on the basis of obtaining the same by way of registered kabala is not binding upon the defendant respondent and that the plaintiffs-petitioners filed Other suit No. 95 of 1992 in the 3rd Sub-Judge Court, Chittagong and the same being decreed against the defendant respondent the F.A. No. 39 of 1995 was preferred by the defendant respondent before the Hon'ble High Court Division which was allowed and against that the petitioner filed C.P. before the Appellate Division which was dismissed affirming the judgment of the F.A No. 39 of 1995 in favour of the defendant respondent and that possession of the plaintiffs-petitioners in the suit land was as the trespasser and for that no title was acquired by the predecessors of the plaintiffs-petitioners and also themselves and that the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata as the same issue was settled by the High Court Division which was subsequently affirmed by the Appellate Division and that the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. The learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong by the judgment and decree dated 30.09.2002 decreed the suit against the defendants-respondents.

6. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 30.09.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong the defendant-respondent No. 1-Zilla Parishad preferred appeal being Other Appeal No. 4 of 2003 before the Court of District Judge, Chittagong and the teamed Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Chittagong by the judgment land decree dated 21.05.2003 dismissed the appeal affirming those passed by the Trial Court.

7. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 21.05.2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Chittagong respondent No.1 preferred Civil Revision No. 2889 of 2003 before the High Court Division and Obtained Rule and upon hearing both the parties a Division Bench of the High Court Division by the judgment and order dated 10.03.2008 made the Rule absolute. The plaintiffs-petitioners being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division.

8. We have heard Mr. Md. Abu Siddique, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioners and perused the judgment and order of the High Court Division and other materials on record. The High Court Division having considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and materials on record found that in the registered deed dated 20th February, 1877 of the suit land there are some overwriting in a few sentences and interpolations and use of separate inks and insertion of a few sentences at the bottom of the deed. Accordingly the High Court Division holds that this deed is a spurious document which was totally overlooked by the courts below. The High Court Division also found that there is no material on record to snow that this deed attracts the suit lands as the plaintiffs-petitioners have not taken steps for repayment of the deed by way of local investigation. The High Court Division also noticed that the claim of acquisition of title on the basis of Exbt. 1 (Ka) to the plaint disproves the plaintiffs' acquisition of title in the suit lands. It has been noticed that admittedly the plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 95 of 1992 in respect of the suit lands which was decreed on 29th January, 1995. Against the said judgment passed by the 1 trial Court the petitioner preferred F.A. No. 39 of 1995 before the High Court Division which was allowed by the judgment and order dated 22nd January, 1998 and the suit was dismissed. Thereupon Civil Petition No. 447 of 1998 was preferred before the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division by the judgment and order dated 1st June, 1998 rejected the leave petition and thereafter the plaintiff petitioner instituted the present suit. The averments made in paragraph 5 of the plaint showed that the plaintiff instituted a suit being Other Class Suit No.95 of 1992 in respect of the suit lands. The High Court Division in the judgment observed that the learned Joint District Judge decreed the Suit No.95 of 1992 to the following effect-“নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বাদী পক্ষেও স্বত্ব স্বার্থ, অধিকার ও দখল আছে মর্মে ঘোষিত হল”. The High Court Division further observed that the courts below not only misread the pleadings and the evidence on record but also made inconsistent observations. The High Court Division found that the plaintiffs themselves admitted that they had instituted a suit earlier in respect of the suit land and lost up to the Appellate Division. The High Court Division in the judgment and decree in F.A. No. 39 of 1995 observed that the plaintiff could not file any paper to show that the alleged raiyat right of Noor Hossain, predecessor of the petitioners either on the basis of settlement or lease taken from the defendant-District Council and further the plaintiff could not file any rent receipt to show that Noor Hossain ever paid rent of the suit land to the defendant-District Council or the District Council ever realized any rent from Noor Hossain the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners. The High Court Division also relied on the decisions of the Appellate Division in Civil Petition No.457 of 1998 where it has been observed- "True but the plaintiffs could not file any paper to show how the alleged raiyati right of Noor Hossain on the basis of settlement or lease taken from defendant No.1. The High Court Division was well founded in law in holding that under the circumstances the plaintiffs have established a case of possession but not title. When they are in possession claiming raiyati settlement they cannot set up adverse possession either. They are not entitled to a declaration of title." The High Court Division having considered the above findings of the Appellate Division; in respect of the subject matter of the suit between the parties and admission of the plaintiffs in the plaint about the misreading of their earlier suit over the same subject matter and examined the question whether the suit is barred by the principles of resjudicata and whether the plaintiff can avoid the plea of resjudicata by adducing new facts. The High Court Division made detailed examination of principles of resjudicata in the facts and circumstances of the case. Having considered the proposition of law in details and the issues involved in the earlier suit and the present suit the High Court Division observed that in the earlier suit the plaintiffs claimed declaration of title and confirmation of possession and in this suit also they claimed similar reliefs besides other reliefs. Having considered all the aspect of the matter the High Court Division rightly found that the substantive reliefs in both the suits are for declaration of title an confirmation of possession in the suit lands. The High Court Division also found that in the instant case the plaintiffs arc admitting in their pleadings about the existence of decisions of the superior courts over the same subject matter and between the same parties. The principle of res judicata is applicable only where Court has in a previous suit or proceedings decided a matter in issue between the same parties. The object of the principle of res judicata as suggested by the expression itself is that finality should impart to judicial decisions and if a case is res judicata, it may not be reopened so as to be adjudged again. The fundamental principle of res judicata is that a question must be finally decided once for all by a competent Court forever between the parties.

9. The High Court Division rightly observed that a litigant can avoid the provisions by taking advantage of Section of the Evidence Act, which defines with precision the ground of such avoidance as fraud or collusion where a party seeks to set aside a decree, no question of yes judicata can arise. But fraud affecting the validity of a decree must be actual positive fraud, a meditated and intentional contrivance to keep the opposite party in ignorance of the real facts of the case. But the High Court Division observed that in the instant case the plaintiff-petitioner did not raise any plea of fraud or collusion paragraph 5 of the plaint. They pleaded that while drawing up the plaint hurriedly, they failed to bring material facts and law in the plaint. This is not a legal ground for avoiding decisions given by proper court having jurisdiction to try the suit which has been finally decided by the apex court of the country.

<u>10. It appears that the High Court Division having considered all the materials on record on correct assessment found that the question of title in the suit lands was directly and substantially in issue between the plaintiffs and the defendant in the earlier suit and decided against the plaintiff’s petitioners. Accordingly the High Court Division also observed to the following effects:</u>

<u>"Since this Court and the Appellate Division clearly found that the plaintiffs failed to establish their title in the suit lands, we cannot sit over those judgments and decide whether or not those decisions were illegal or erroneous. The suit is apparently barred under Section 11. C.P.C. and therefore, the same are liable to be dismissed. The Courts below on a misconception of law and fact held that the suit was not barred by the principles of res judicata. The suit is not legally maintainable and the judgment of the Courts below to be interfered with."</u>

11. With the aforesaid findings and observation the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute. In view of the above findings and observation we do not find any merit in the leave petition.

12. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1301 of 2015.
lawyer:

For Respondent Nos.11-16. Not represented.
parties:
