full_judgment:
Mr. Muhammad Imman Ali, J.:- This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 08.12.2014 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 26 of 2011 making the Rule absolute.

2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that the respondent Nos. 1-10 as plaintiffs filed title Suit No. 1 of 1998 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola, for declaration of title in the suit land with further declaration that the order dated 30.12.1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 described in schedule `Kha' to the is plaint illegal, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs. They stated inter alia that the suit land measuring 00810 `shahashranqsha' of Mouja Char Toffazzel, C.S. Khatian No. 4205/6 was khas land of the Government and the father of the plaintiffs, namely Abdul Mannan took settlement of the said land from the Government on payment of salami and has been possessing the same by running business thereon and that after the death of the plaintiff's father they inherited the said land but having failed to take steps, the khatian could not be prepared in their names. Subsequently, they filed an application in the office of the defendant No.  3 for a new khatian in the name of the plaintiffs, and accordingly a Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 was started. Defendant No. 3 asked defendants No. 1 to inquire into the matter and submit a report, but defendant Nos. 4 and 5 in collusion with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 managed to submit a false report .While defendant Nos. 4 and 5 tried to grab the property, defendant No. 3 by his order dated 30.12.1997 started 4 proceeding of a miscellaneous case to grant re-settlement. The said order is illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs and that defendant Nos.  4and 5 demolished their shop room on 03.10.2002 and forcibly erected two small houses on 28.10.2002, and hence the suit. By a subsequent amendment of the plaint they added a prayer for evicting defendant Nos. 4 and 5 upon demolishing the two huts erected by them on the suit land.

3. Defendant Nos. 1-3 and 4-5 contested the suit by filling two separate written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint.

4. The case of defendant Nos. 4-5 in brief is that the suit land is khas land of the Government and that the said Land having fallen vacant for a long time, these defendants erected a tin-shed house thereon in 1976 these defendants on 23.08.1994 approached the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Char Fashion, Bhola for permanent settlement or in the alternative, for year to year lease of the said land in their favour resulting in the initiation of Settlement Case No. 289F/96-97 and 290F/96-97: that the plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bhola for cancellation of the said settlement case, which was rejected by order dated 30.12.1997 and the proposal for year to year lease of the suit land in favour of the defendants was approved and the defendants paid lease money and obtained DCR and have been running business therein and the plaintiffs neither took settlement of the suit land nor did they run any business therein and hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. Defendant Nos. 1-3 in their written statement stated, inter alia that the suit land is the khas land of the Government and that no settlement case was initiated in the name of the plaintiffs and that the order dated 30.12.1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 is just and legal and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Bhola. Leased out the suit land in favour of the defendant Nos. 4-5 in connection with Miscellaneous Case Nos. 289/97-98 and 290/97-98 and that in order to grab the suit land, the plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95-96 which was rejected because the suit is liable to be dismissed.

6. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence and materials on record the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Char Fashion, Bhola by his judgment and decree dated 04.09.2005.

7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs preferred Title Appeal No. 03 of 2006before the District Judge, Bhola and the said appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, Second Court, Bhola, who by his judgment and decree dated 30.05.2007 dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

8. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 26 of 2011 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule which upon hearing the parties was made absolute on 08.12.2014. Hence, the defendants as petitioners are now before us having filed instant civil petition for leave to appeal.

9. Mr. Saifuddin Ahmed Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the Courts below after due consideration of averments made in the plaint, the evidence adduced by the parties and record of the settlement case having found that the settlement case in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs did not attain finally with the payment of entire amount of salami and the execution of kabuliyat, rightly held that by virtue of the settlement case, no title in respect of the suit property had been conferred upon the plaintiffs and as such High Court Division erred in law setting aside the judgment and decree of the Courts below without adverting to the land said concurrent findings. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in misreading and misinterpretation of the observation made by the lower appellate Court that, “বাদীপক্ষের পূর্ববর্তী আ: মান্নানের নামে ভূমি বাবদ ১৫৭/৫০-৫১ নং গ্রুপ সেটেলমেন্ট কেস রুজু থাকায় এবং তিনি পরবর্তীতে সেলামীর টাকা পরিশোধ করার নিমিত্ত আবশ্যকীয় প্রতিকার প্রার্থনা যুক্তে বাদী পক্ষের আদালতের স্মরণাপন্ন হওয়া যুক্তিযুক্ত ও সংগত ছিল।” In as such as admittedly the settlement case having not been finally concluded with the payment of entire amount of salami and the execution of Kabuliyat with the establishment of land lord and tenant relationship, no title in respect of the suit property was conferred upon the plaintiffs and hence, they are not entitled to get any relief by way of declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in the suit property. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute declaring title of the plaintiffs in the suit property who are admittedly out of possession inasmuch as a party out of possession cannot get any r decree for declaration of title without a decree for khas possession.

10. Mr. S. N. Goswami, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

11. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

<u>12. In the impugned judgment the High Court Division observed that the selfsame disputed property was the subject matter in Civil Revision No. 3800 of 2007 wherein the High Court Division remanded the case to the appellate Court for passing fresh judgment after considering the genuineness of the plaintiffs claim of settlement from the Government and for proper adjudication into the matter of controversy. Upon considering the available record of the group settlement case the lower appellate Court found the existence of the group settlement case. The High Court Division noted that only part of the original papers were sent and not the whole case record. The High Court Division observed that the lower appellate Court was misconceived in appreciating the actual provision of law and has failed to evaluate the evidence on record in its totality. The findings suffer from contradiction and lack of proper appreciation of the evidence on record. Further the High Court Division observed that the fact remains that the Government admits that the suit land was settled with plaintiffs predecessor by Group Settlement Case No. 157-F/50-51 and accordingly, K.M. settlement was done and in that case four persons, including the predecessor of the plaintiffs, obtained settlement and that the plaintiffs possessed the land from the time of settlement of their predecessor-in-interest since 1957. The High Court Division also noted that the only witness adduced from the side of the defendants was a formal witness, who could not say whether the group settlement case was started or that Abdul Mannan, the predecessor of the plaintiffs was one of the settlement holders.</u>

Thus, the High Court Division found that the Courts below failed to assess the evidence on record and wrongly decided the original suit and that the plaintiffs properly discharged by adequate credible evidence their contention as made in the plaint.

13. We note from the impugned judgment that High Court of has merely. decreed the suit of the plaintiffs declaring the plaintiff's title to the suit land, but has not come to any finding or decision with regard to the plaintiffs second prayer concerning the order dated 30.12.1997 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 92/95- 96.

In view of the discussion of the High Court Division upon assessment of the evidence and material on record we do not find that the impugned judgment calls for any interference by, this Division.

14. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.

full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. This petition at the instance of the judgment debtor is directed from a judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 8829 of 2009 discharging the rule.

2. Facts leading to this leave petition are that the National Bank Limited, Kawran Bazar Branch obtained a decree for a sum of Tk. 7,67,845.51 on 22.11.2004 against the petitioner and his company. The decree holder put the decree into execution in Artha Rin Execution Case No.65 of 2005. Thereafter, the Artha Rin Adalat published proclamation of auction sale for realising the decretal amount of Tk. 7,67,11,845,51 by selling the mortgaged property of three bighas four kathas land situated at Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka. The property was ultimately sold to the highest bidder at Tk. 7,75,50,600/-, Against the said sale the petitioner filed an application for setting aside the sale on two grounds namely the sale was held at a very low price and that he was willing to pay the entire auction money. The Artha Rin Adalat by order dated 25.8.2009 rejected the prayer.

<u>3. The decree holder contested the rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition stating inter alia that the judgment debtor having failed to pay the total dues it filed the execution proceedings. His company filed Writ Petition No. 6793 of 2005 and the rule was discharged. Thereafter, he moved this court in Civil Petition No. 681 of 2005 which was also dismissed. Thereafter, he filed another application under Order 21 rule 90 for setting aside the sale. The executing court rejected the said application. Thereafter, he filed another miscellaneous appeal before the High Court Division and the High Court Division dismissed the said appeal. This order was also affirmed by this Division. A review petition was also filed and the review petition was also dismissed. Thereafter, another writ petition was also filed by the judgment debtor No. 8 Mahbuba Kabir Chowdhury which was also dismissed by the High Court Division and this court affirmed the said judgment. The judgment debtors having exhausted all the remedies available they are not legally entitled to any relief. The auction purchaser also contested the rule and claimed that he being the highest bidder, his bid was accepted and a boinama was also executed in his favour. Under such circumstances there is no scope of interfering with the matter.</u>

4. Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmood, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has drawn our attention to the order-sheet of the execution case and submitted that a gigantic fraud has been practiced by the auction purchaser in connivance with the officers of the decree holder bank in securing the auction sale and this will be evident on the face of the order-sheet. He argued that this fraud is sufficient enough to set aside the sale and the Adalat erred therefore in accepting the bid money of the auction purchaser, inasmuch as, in presence of filling an application by the decree holder bank to issue certificate conferring title of the mortgaged property on the ground that the highest bidder has offered a price which is shocking low, the court cannot accept the bid of the auction purchaser. Dr. Kamal Hossain appearing for the auction purchaser strongly opposed the contention and submitted that this petition should be rejected outright without even looking at the alleged fraud. According to him, there is no scope for looking at the merit of the matter, inasmuch as if the principles of resjudicata is applicable in a case it is one of the fittest case to apply this principle. Dr. Hossain has drawn our attention to the chronological applications and writ petitions unsuccessfully moved by the judgment debtors and submitted that all those applications were rejected up to the highest court, and thereafter, there is ho scope to reopen the said issue.

5. True, if one looks at the petitions moved on behalf of the judgment debtors certainly there will be no hesitation to infer an adverse presumption against the judgment debtors that their conduct disentitle them to any relief from the Court. There is no doubt that the finalization of the auction sale has been withheld at the instance of the judgment debtors on many occasions. The petitioner moved Writ Petition No. 6793 of 2005 and then Miscellaneous Case No. 24 of 2005. His wife also moved Miscellaneous Case No. 302 of 2008, Writ Petition No. 8242 of 2008 and then the petitioner moved Writ Petition No. 8829 of 2009 against different orders. Another writ petition was also filed by Mahbuba Kabir in 2010. Against the judgments of those matters, they unsuccessfully moved this court, in different civil petitions and miscellaneous petitions.

6. The High Court Division in discharging the rule has observed that the order of auction sale has been finally decided by this court in favour of auction purchaser, and therefore, there is no scope to entertain another application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. It further held that the petitioner did not pay the total decretal amount before the auction sale and after auction sale was confirmed, and a boinama was registered, there is no scope to entertain such frivolous application. It further held that the Artha Rin Adalat on consideration of the entire materials on record by a detailed order having rejected the application, the auction sale is not void or illegal and that after the confirmation of the auction sale, there is no scope to invoke inherent power for setting aside the auction sale.

7. As observed above, in the face of the judgment of the High Court Division it cannot be said that it is not justified in discharging the rule, but the point that has been raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is totally a legal point which cannot be ignored altogether. The High Court Division has ignored the power given to an Adalat by the Ain for securing justice in a given case. It appeared that the auction purchaser submitted tender at Tk. 7,75,00,600/- and two other bidders Md. Abdul Aziz at Tk. 1,00,60,000/- and Nasimul Gani at TK. 50,00,000/-, The Artha Rin Adalat rejected the bids on 29.06.2005 on the reasoning that the price was shockingly low and that the proclamation of sale was not published in the locality. The decree holder again prayed for selling the property in auction under section 33(4) of the Ain. This time also three bidders, the auction purchaser submitted tender at Tk. 7,75,50,600/-, the second bidder Md. Abdul Aziz at Tk. 1,01,00,000/- and the third bidder Md. Rojob An at Tk. 40,00,000/-. This time the Adalat was of the view that the money offered by the highest bidder is higher than the bank's claim of Tk. 7,67,11,845.51 and therefore, despite filing an application under section 33(7) for issuing a certificate conferring title by the decree-holder, in the absence of opposition in accepting the highest bid, the prayer for issuing certificate is rejected. Accordingly it directed the auction purchaser to deposit the balance amount.

8. Same auction purchaser submitted his first bid at Tk. 7,75,50,600/- and the Adalat rejected his bid on the reasoning that the amount was shockingly low. In the second bid he submitted tender exactly at the same price of Tk. 7,75,50,600/- with the difference of only fifty thousand more than his first bid. Two other bidders also submitted almost at similar price. How one can believe that this sale is not collusive, where the highest bid is at over seven crore taka, the second bid is at taka one crore and the third bid is around taka fifty lacs. The second bidder is the same person and the third bidder is although another person, it cannot altogether be ignored that this third bidder is none but the one set up by the auction purchaser. Thus there is no gainsaying that the auction purchaser submitted three bids, one in his name and other persons have been set up by him in order to show that there was complaisance of formalities, but in order to avoid the deposit of huge money along with the bids as required by law a very low amount was quoted by two bidders. Secondly, if the highest bidder's first bid is found shockingly low price, how can the court accept the second bid at an amount which is almost the similar price? More so, as per law also the court cannot accept any bid if the decree holder prays for conferring title under section 33(7) of the Act, which read as follows:

" (৭) উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও, ডিক্রীদার, উল্লিখিত সম্পত্তি মালিকানা সত্ত্বে পাইতে আগ্রহী মর্মে আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালতের নিকট লিখিতভাবে আবেদন করিলে, আদালত, [উপ-ধারা(১), (২) (২ক), (২গ) ও (৩) এর বিধানাবলীর কোনরূপ হানি না ঘটাইয়া, উপ-ধারা (৪) ও (৫) এর কার্যক্রম অনুসরণ করা হইতে বিরত থাকিবে; এবং ডিক্রীদারের প্রার্থীতমতে উল্রেখিত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ব ডিক্রীদারের অনুকূলে ন্যস্ত হইয়াছে মর্মে ঘোষনা প্রদান পূর্বক তৎমর্মে একটি সনদপত্র জারি করিবে এবং জারিকৃত এইরূপ সনদপত্র সত্ত্বের দলিল হিসাবে হন্য হইবে; আদালত উহার একটি অনুলিপি সংশ্লিষ্ট স্থানীয় সাব-রেজিস্ট্রারের অফিসে নিবন্ধনের জন্য প্রেরণ করিবে। "

9. It says that if the decree holder is willing to take a certificate conferring title in his favour, the Adalat shall abstain from proceeding with the auction sale and shall declare that the property vests in favour of the decree holder and shall issue a certificate which shall be treated as title deed. The law is so clear that whenever the decree holder files an application praying for conferring the title of the mortgaged property on the ground that the price quoted by the auction purchaser is shockingly low, the Adalat is left with no option but to issue certificate. The decree holder though filed petition for conferring title in its favour did not oppose the acceptance of the highest bid. The Adalat in the premises accepted the bid observing that since the price quoted by the auction purchaser is higher than the amount claimed by the bank, the prayer of the decree holder is rejected. This is not a legal ground to reject the prayer for issuing certificate. The filing of an application under section 33(7) presupposes that price quoted by the auction purchaser was shockingly low and therefore, the decree holder is not willing to accept the bid money. The court in such case cannot accept the tender of the highest bidder.

10. It is understandable from the above facts that why the decree holder bank did not oppose in the acceptance of the bid money quoted by the highest bidder despite praying for conferring title of the property in its favour. The bank officials in connivance with the auction purchaser did not press the application filed under section 33(7) of the Ain. Admittedly, the mortgaged property is situated at Tejgaon Industrial Area in the heart of the city and though it is called an industrial area, almost all big business houses have set up their corporate head offices in that area, and the area of the land is over three bights Under no stretch of imagination the price of the land would be at seven crore and odd for such areas of land in such a posh area. That is why though the judgment debtors prayer was rejected on different occasions, as soon as, the petitioner knew that the property was sold at taka seven crow and odd, he wanted to deposit the said amount. Though the executing court rejected the earlier tender on the ground of low price, on the second occasion, it has accepted the bid amount which is almost similar amount of the earlier one within a space of two months and that's too, in presence of an application under section 33(7) for conferring title on the ground of inadequacy of price.

<u>11. Recently we have been noticing in good number of cases that whenever any mortgaged property is sold in execution of a decree, the bank officials in connivance with the auction purchasers sell them at low price that results in multifariousness of proceedings. Even in cases where the sale price is much lower than the total decretal amount, the decree holders did not oppose the sale and take steps to realise the balance amount on liquidation of personal bonds taken from the judgment debtors. This practice leads to third generation litigations. This has caused due to advancing excessive money by means of over valuation of the mortgaged property than the actual value by corruptible means. Whenever, the judgment debtors failed to pay the total outstanding dues, the decree-holders sold the mortgaged property at a low price and then they resorted to other proceedings with a view to recover the balance outstanding amount to cover up their misdeeds. We have been noticing this type of irregularities in most auction sales that resulted in huge amount of loans, remain unpaid with the commercial banks and multiplicity proceedings crop up. This illegal practices should be checked otherwise the banks will be burdened with heavy outstanding liabilities for the aches and corrupt practices by its officials.</u>

<u>12. On perusal of the orders dated 29.6.2005 and 28.8.2005, we have no hesitation to hold the view that the mortgaged property was sold at a shockingly low price in violation of section 33(7) of the Ain. As regards the question of resjudicata, when a party against whom a judgment is offered in evidence may prove that the judgment or order has been obtained or the sale has been conducted by practicing fraud, the court will not hesitate to cancel the sale or declare nullity of the judgment. Fraud is a ground for nullifying a judgment and it can be raised or set up in a collateral proceeding to show that a decree or order obtained by the decree holder against the judgment debtor was by practicing fraud or collusion. Fraud includes all acts, commissions and concealments which involve a breach of equitable duty, trust and are injurious to another or by which an undue and unconscious advantage is taken by another. If in the face of the order fraud is detected the court will not hesitate to exercise its power to nullify the action. It is a nullity in the eye of law. More so, a decision cannot constitute a bar on the principle of resjudicata when new circumstances have come to exist which require a reappraisal of the true legal position of law.</u>

<u>13. An appraisal of the provisions of the Ain will reveal the intention of the legislature to promulgate the law. This Ain has been enacted with an object to recover the outstanding dues from the bank defaulters who are unable to pay loans through a speedier process. This law has been amended many a times but by the same time the legislature was not oblivious of the hardship being faced by the genuine borrowers in the repayment of the banks liabilities and as a result though it has promulgated a special law, it has included some provisions which discourage the Adalats to pass decree or to sell the mortgaged property by resorting to stream of justice. A detail provisions for resolving the dispute by applying the alternative dispute resolution system (ADR) have been stipulated and the legislature has encouraged to follow such method. Even after filing of an execution case, a provision has been provided for resolving the dispute by ADR. The provisions, of the Code of Civil Procedure are applicable for execution of a decree, but then also, there is a provision for filing objection by a third party against the decree or order of sale of mortgaged property. Though there are some stringent provisions contained in the Ain on the question of auction sale, appeal, revision, detention in civil prison, there are provisions for making interlocutory orders by the Adalat if it finds that such order is necessary for securing the ends of justice. Even after failure of two successive ADRs, a non-obstante clause has been provided in section 45 of the Ain empowering the Adalat to afford the parties to resolve the dispute amicably at any stage. This shows the intention of the legislature that despite the sale of the property if the execution case is not finally disposed of, the Adalat has power to resolve the matter even at a later stage of the proceedings for ends of justice. Section 45 reads:</u>

<u>" ৪৫। (১) এই আইনের কোন কিছুই, বিচার কার্যক্রমের পরবর্তী যে কোন পর্যায়ে, কোন মামলার আপোষ নিষ্পত্তি করা হইতে পক্ষগণকে বারিত করিবে না।"</u>

<u>(২) উপ-ধারা(১) এর অধীনে প্রদত্ত মামলার আপোষ নিষ্পত্তির সুযোগ এই আইনে মামলা নিষ্পত্তির জন্য ব্যবস্থিত অন্যান্য পদ্ধতি এবং নির্ধারিত সময়সীমার হানি বা ব্যত্যয় ঘটাইতে পারবে না।</u>

<u>14. It is stated in Craies on Statute Law, Seventh Edn, that in a court of law or equity, what the legislature intended to be done or not to be done can be legitimately ascertained from what it has chosen to enact, either in express words or by reasonable and unnecessary implication. The statutes imposing import duties must be r interpreted in the light of their object i.e. to protect home producer. A statute, even more than a contract, must be construed, utres magis valeat quam pereat, that is, it is better for a thing to have effect than to be made void. So the intention of the legislature may not be treated as vain or left to operate in the air. If a statute is passed for the purpose of enabling something to be done, but omits to mention in terms some detail which is of great importance to the proper and effectual performance of the work which the statute has in contemplation, the courts are at liberty to infer that the statute by implication empowers that detail to be carried out.</u>

<u>15. Section 49 authorizes the Adalat to pass appropriate order that if it deems fit on the application of the judgment debtor to afford him to pay the decretal amount by four equal installments in a year. Even if the decree-holder agrees, the Adalat may allow to repay the dues within three years in twelve equal installments, Section 57 of the Ain is another enabling provision empowering the Adalat to pass any order for securing the ends of justice. This provision has been added after enumerating the above provisions discussed above. It is a power to act ex debito justitiae to do that real and substantial justice for the administration of which alone it exists or to prevent the abuse of the process of the court. It lengthens the hands of the Adalat to pass any order to do justice when there is no other remedy open to the aggrieved party. When the Ain itself recognizes the existence of the inherent power of the Adalat, there is no question of implying any powers out side the limits of the Ain. (See Monohar Lal Chopera V. Rai Bahadur Rao, AIR 1962 SC 527)</u>

<u>16. There is no doubt that this power can be exercised sparingly it is a power to promote justice and prevent abuse of the process of the court but if the Adalat finds that by practicing fraud or by false representation, a party has obtained a judgment or order, the Adalat can always interfere, and even the argument of functus officio cannot stand on its way to pass such orders which may advance justice to a party. (Abdul Aziz V. Abani Mohan, 30 DLR (AD) 221, Bangladesh V. Khair Bhuiyan, 55 DLR (AD) 76. A court can set aside an execution case if it is found that a party by practicing fraud obtained an amendment of a decree to get over the bar of limitation and got possession. [M. Majid V. Iqbal Bahar, 2000 BLD 285, affirmed in 5 BLC (AD) 7].</u>

17. Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmood, learned counsel has drawn our attention to certain documents produced by way of supplementary paper book and submitted that from before the date of auction sale the judgment debtor was on critical condition. His kidneys were completely damaged. He was hospitalized for a long time and as his condition deteriorated he was taken to Bangkok by air ambulance. Ultimately, his kidneys were transplanted in Singapore. The medical, documents show that the judgment debtor's kidneys were transplanted in Singapore. It is submitted that due to his critical condition, the judgment debtor was economically crippled and could not take proper steps in the proceedings earlier and even then, when he came to know that the property was sold at a very low price he offered to purchase at taka eight crore, but he could not deposit the amount within the stipulated time. Mr. Mahmud submits that this was due to his ailment.

18. "On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the matter, this court has no reason to doubt that the auction sale was held by practicing fraud upon the court, and therefore, the auction sale must be declared illegal despite previous judgments. However, we noticed that the suit was instituted in 2003 and it was decreed on 22-11-2004. The execution case was filed in 2005. If the auction sale is set aside the decree holder bank will be burdened with litigation, the auction purchaser will also sustain economic loss immensely, and multifariousness of proceedings may be cropped up. The auction purchaser has spent Tk. 7,75,50,600/- in September 2005, the price of the amount even though low, but no doubt it is a colossal amount. We have considered the loss that may be sustained by him if the sale is set aside. He has collected this amount from different sources and is the event of setting aside the sale he may be subjected to huge financial loss due to blockade of this amount for about eleven years. If he had invested the said amount towards other business, he might have earned about threefold times of the said amount. Considering the balance of convenience and inconvenience, we are constrained to hold that instead of setting aside the sale if he is compensated by the judgment debtor, ends of justice will be met since the judgment debtor was willing to pay more than the sale price.

19. Accordingly we wanted to know from the learned counsel of the petitioner to intimate the court as to whether the judgment debtor will be able to pay Tk. 32,00,00,000/- crore to the auction purchaser which is four times higher than the amount spent. We also proposed to the auction purchaser through his learned counsel as to whether the auction purchaser is ready to accept taka thirty two crore a if the judgment debtor agrees to pay the said amount before we proceed to set aside the sale. Accordingly, the matter was adjourned. Both the learned counsel later on accepted our proposal.

20. Mr. Rokonuddin Mahmood, however, submits that during this month of Ramadan and ahead of ensuing Eid, it would be difficult for the judgment-debtor to collect such huge amount of money and therefore prayed that the judgment-debtor should be afforded an opportunity to pay the amount by three installments on humanitarian consideration. Considering his difficulty we direct the judgment-debtor to deposit taka ten crore by 31st August, 2016 and the balance amount by two equal instruments on 29th September and 30th October, 2016 respectively in the executing court without fail. If the judgment-debtor fails to deposit any of the installments as above within the stipulated time, the auction sale shall stand valid. We direct the Artha Rin Adalat to allow the auction purchaser to withdraw the money to be deposited by the judgment debtor from the court.

21. On depositing the entire amount of thirty two crore, the auction sale, the boinama, the judgments and decrees, and the order confirming sale shall render void automatically and the judgment debtor's right, title and interest in the mortgaged property shall restore as before. It is also directed that the decree-holder and the auction purchaser shall hand over the title deeds in respect of the property forthwith as soon as the judgment-debtors liquidated the debt of thirty two crore by 30th October, 2016. We also direct the Artha Rin Adalat to withhold the withdrawal of the final installment if the auction purchaser/decree holder does not deposit the title deeds in the Adalat.

22. We would like to observe here that upon payment of the said amount, the judgment debtors will be relinquished from the liabilities in respect of the mortgaged property. This petition is disposed of with the above observations, findings and directions.

End.

full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain, J. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.08.2009 passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2494 of 2006 discharging the rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 10.04.2006 passed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 239 of 2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 22.07.2005 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 30 of 2005. The facts, leading to the filing of this civil petition for Leave to Appeal, in brief, are:

2. Respondent Nos. 1-11 as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 180 of 2004 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, First Court, Gazipur for declaration of title and recovery of Khas possession in the suit land measuring an area of 01 decimal impleading petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 12 as defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Their case, in short, is that the suit land originally belonged to Amiruddin alias Aminuddin and Jamiruddin in equal shares and accordingly, the R.S. Khatian was prepared. The suit land described in the schedule to the plaint fell in the Saham of Aminuddin, who died leaving behind three sons, namely, Moslehuddin alias Moslemuddin Nurul Islam and Dalilur Rahman. The suit land was subsequently recorded in their names at the time of R.S. operation. Moslemuddin, Nurul Islam and Daliolur Rahman sold the suit land to the plaintiffs' predecessor-in-interest Serajuddin by a registered deed of sale dated 19.08.1974 and inducted the vendee into the possession of the land. After that, Serajuddin died leaving behind the plaintiffs as his heirs. Plaintiffs' further case is that the defendants forcibly dispossessed them from the suit land at the beginning of 1999 and erected a shop thereon. The plaintiffs requested the defendants several times to handover the vacant possession of the suit land but to no avail. Hence the plaintiffs were constrained to file the title suit. Defendant No. 2 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint stating inter alia, that the plaintiffs' suit is not maintainable in its present form and it is bad for defect of parties.

3. After hearing the parties, the trial Court by its Judgment and order dated 12.07.2005 decreed the suit with costs against defendant No. 2 on contest and ex-parte against defendant No. 1.

4. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, defendant No. 2 preferred Title Appeal No. 239 of 2005 before the learned District Judge, Gazipur, who by his judgment and order dated 10.04.2006 dismissed the appeal affirming the Judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree of the appellate Court, defendant No. 2 preferred a revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2494 of 2006. After hearing the parties, the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, by his Judgment and order dated 26.08.2009 discharged the Rule affirming the judgments and decrees passed by the appellate Court as well as the trial Court.

6. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the defendant-leave-petitioner has filed this civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

7. Mr. Md. Nur Hossain Chowdhury, learned Advocates, appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner, submits that the plaintiffs could not prove that the suit has been filed within six months from the alleged dated of dispossession as contemplated under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act and as such, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. He further submits that the suit land is vague and indefinite and that all the courts including the High Court Division failed to notice this aspect of the case and as such, impugned the judgment delivered by the High Court Division should be set aside.

8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate, perused the impugned judgment and the materials on record.

<u>9. The High Court Division came to a finding that admittedly, the plaintiff filed the suit seeking declaration of title and recovery of possession under section 42 of the specific Relief Act, and that under Article 142 of the specific relief Act, the period for filing the suit was 12 years from the date of dispossession and that the contention of the leaned Advocate for the defendants that the plaintiffs failed to institute the suit within 6 months from the alleged dated of dispossession under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act was not tenable in the eye of law. The High Court Division further found that the suit land measuring .01 acre appertained to R.S. plot No. 148 and that the plaintiff and defendant No. 2 admitted that fact and as such, there was no dispute regarding identity of the suit land.</u>

<u>10. The findings of the High Court Division having been made on proper appreciation of law and fact do not call for interference. Accordingly, this civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.</u>

End.

full_judgment:
Abdul Wahhab Miah, J. This Civil petition for leave to appeal has been filed by the defendants against the judgment and order dated the 12th day of August, 2010 passed by a learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3260 of 2008 discharging the Rule.

<u>2. Short facts necessary for disposal of this petition are that respondent Nos. 1-25 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 26 of 1991 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Chandpur for partition of the Suit land measuring an area of 1.42 acres. The petitioners who were defendant Nos. 6-9, 26 and 31-34 filed written statement, but eventually they did not contest the suit and the suit was decreed in preliminary form on 28.11.2002 on contest against defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and ex-parte against the other defendants including the petitioners. Against the said decree, the petitioners filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) giving rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 41 of 2003 Miscellaneous case was rejected on 15.04.2004 as being not maintainable. In the order, the learned Joint District Judge observed that since final decree was not drawn till then the petitioner could seek saham in the partition suit which was still in the form of preliminary decree and that there was scope to amend or alter the saham of the parties allotted in the preliminary decree. Thereafter, the petitioners filed an application for giving them saham. The trial Court rejected the prayer on the ground that after giving saham to the plaintiffs there was no land from which saham could be given. The same view has been affirmed by the District Judge in Civil Revision No. 10 of 2006 filed under section 115(2) of the Code. Being aggrieved by the said order of the District Judge, the petitioner, the petitioner preferred civil revision before the High Court Division being No. 3264 of 2009 under section 115(4) of the code. The High Court Division also took the same view at the same time it observed:</u>

<u>"In the instant case, since the decree is in preliminary form and final decree is yet to be drawn up, the petitioner can prefer appeal against the preliminary decree. On perusal of the record it is also apparent that the petitioners suffered for no fault of them but in view of the provision of law and the decision referred above, I am of the opinion that their proper remedy lies in the Court of appeal against the preliminary decree which can be filed any time before final decree is drawn up"</u>

3. In view of the observation of the High Court Division quoted hereinbefore, we do not find any reason on the part of the petitioner to file this leave petition.

4. Be that as it may, we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division calling for interference by this Court. Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 20.05.2010 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 836 of 1991)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal arises out of the judgment and Order dated 20.05.2010 respondent. No.1 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Appeal No.836 of 1991, dismissing the appeal, affirming the judgment and decree dated 28.01.1991 of the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Comilla in Artha Rin Case No.123 of 1990 decreeing the case in part granting simple interest at the rate of 6% per anum from the date of filing till the date of the decree.

<u>2. The facts relevant for disposal of this petition, in brief, are that the respondent No.1 (defendant No.1 in the Artha Rin Case) took loan of Tk.3,94,000/- under the "Power of Driving Vehicle Scheme, 1987" from the Sonali Bank Limited. Kangshanagar Branch, Comilla (plaintiff in the Artha Rin Case and petitioner herein). The loan was taken to purchase a bus and in due course the bus plied on the permitted route the respondent No. 1 duly paid the bank's installments, but could not continue to do so as the bus was not yielding sufficient income. Due to the failure of respondent No.1 to pay the loan as stipulated in the loan agreement, the petitioner filed Money Suit No. 19 of 1987 in the Court of 1st Subordinate Judge, Comilla for a sum of Tk.6,25,486.05, being the loan amount and accrued interest thereon. The respondent No.1 filed written statement admitting that he took the loan of Tk.3,94,000/- but denied the amount claimed by the Bank in the Money Suit. He expressed his intention to pay back the loan while explaining the reasons for his inability to pay the bank's installments in due time. At the same time he prayed that the installment may be fixed by the Court at Tk.5,000/- per month. In due course the case was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat and renumbered as Artha Rin Case No.123 of 1990. The respondent No.1, being absent when the matter was taken up for hearing, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 28.01.1991. The suit was decreed for the full claim with interest at the rate of 6% per anum from the date of filing till the date of decree. The respondent No.1 thereafter filed Miscellaneous Case No.07 of 1991 with the prayer for setting aside the ex-parte decree. The petitioner filed an objection in the miscellaneous case. After hearing both the parties, by judgment and order dated 29.06.1991, the miscellaneous case was, allowed on condition that the applicants deposit Tk.50,000/- within 30 days and file the receipt in Court, failing which the application for restoration would be deemed to have been rejected. The deposit having not been made within the period stipulated by the Court, the decree was drawn up on 30.07.1991. The petitioner-Bank thereafter preferred First Appeal No.836 of 1991 claiming that the interest ordered by the trial Court at 6% per anum was too low and prayed that the interest may be ordered to be paid at 16% per anum till realization of the claimed amount. By the impugned judgment and order dated 20.05.2010 a Division Bench of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal, hence the instant leave petition.</u>

3. Mr. M.A. Sobhan, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the award of interest at the rate of 6% per anum is patently illegal and interest should have been awarded at the rate of 16% per anum. He further submits that the finding of the High Court Division that waiting from 1991 till the middle of 2010 to prosecute the case showed collusion of Sonali Bank, is unwarranted and untenable.

4. We heard the respondent No.1, Mr. Abdul Malek, who appeared in person. He stated before the Court that he was wilting to pay the Bank dues, but could not do so due to the fact that his route permit had been withdrawn, and his bus was off the road.

<u>5. We have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and respondent No. 1 in person and perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division as well as the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. The High Court Division has observed that this matter has been pending since 1991 and Sonali Bank took no action to prosecute the case and if the Bank had accepted the decree when it was pronounced then by this time they would have received more money than the money which has accrued from the award of a lesser rate of interest. This is what we understand from the judgment of the High Court Division, which found no merit in the appeal.</u>

6. Having considered all the matters, we are of the view that this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal has no merit and is, accordingly dismissed, without, however, any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 17.04.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.838 of 2008)
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain J. This petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution of Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.04.2008 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.838 of 2008 making the Rule absolute.

2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No.433 of 2006 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka against the respondent impleading them as defendants praying for declaration that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit property; that the exparte decree dated 26.04.1989 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.291 of 1985 is void, fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff; that the deed being No.6659 dated 30.08.1989 registered at the office of the Sub-Registrar, Mirpur, Dhaka in respect of the suit property in favour of the defendant No.1 is void, fraudulent, without consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff; that the case was subsequently transferred to the Court of Additional Joint District Judge, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No.47 of 2007.

3. The present petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.291 of 1985 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against Syed Rafiuddin Ahmed as defendant No.1 and Government of the Peoples' Republic of Bangladesh as defendant No.2. The suit was decreed exparte on 24.06.1989. The petitioner filed Title Execution Case No.45 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for executing the decree and in the said execution case kabala was executed by the Court on 28.08.1989 and was registered on 30.09.1989. In the meantime, the present petitioner Most. Shahida Khanam as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.288 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge challenging the exparte decree. Eventually the suit No.288 of 1989 was withdrawn with permission to sue afresh. Thereafter the petitioner filed Title Suit No.291 of 1992 in the same Court praying for a declaration that the exparte judgment and decree dated 28.08.1989 passed in Title Suit No.291 of 1992 on being transferred to the Court of Assistant Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No.39 of 1993. The suit was decreed by the trial court by judgment and decree dated 29.01.1994. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court the respondent filed title Appeal No.67 of 1994 before the Court of District Judge, Dhaka and the appeal was allowed setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree of the appellate Court below the petitioner filed Civil Revision No.2310 of 1996 before the High Court Division and the Rule in the said Civil Revision was made absolute by judgment and order dated 17.05.2001 setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below restoring those passed by the trial Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order 17.05.2001 passed by the High Court Division the respondent filed a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division and leave having been granted gave rise to Civil Appeal No.361 of 2002. The Appellate Division by the judgment and order dated 08.05.2006 allowed the appeal and thus the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division was set aside and the suit was barred by resjudicata and limitation .

5. In allowing the appeal the Appellate Division observed that: "Title Suit No.291 of 1992 filed seeking declaration in respect of the decree passed in the suit for specific performance of contract without consequential relief in respect of the kabala that was obtained on execution of the decree passed in the suit for specific performance of contract on our view the said suit was not maintainable." The Appellate Division also found that the plaintiff was required to file the suit for removal of the cloud cast on the plaintiffs title by the kabala dated 30.12.1989.in pursuant to the decree obtained by the present petitioner. Accordingly the Appellate Division further observed that the plaintiff having had not sought for the consequential relief in the light of the provision of Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, the plaintiffs suit was not maintainable. High Court Division erred in law in setting aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court. Accordingly the appeal was allowed by the Appellate Division. After disposal of the said Civil Appeal petitioner filed Title Suit No.433 of 2006 in the Court of Joint District judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka impleading the present respondent and the Government of Bangladesh as defendants praying for a declaration that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the suit property and that the exparte decree dated 26.04.1989 passed in No. 261 of 1985 in void and not binding upon the plaintiff and that the deed No. 6659 dated 30.08.1989 in respect or suit property in favour of the defendant No. 1 is void inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff and the said suit on transfer to the court of Additional joint District Judge was remember as title suit No. 47 of 2007.

6. In the above suit the plaintiff petitioner tiled an application under section 151 C.P.C. for temporary injunction praying for restraining the present respondent from proceeding with Title Execution Case No.45 of 1989 pending in the Court of Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka levied for execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.291 of 1985. The application was opposed by the respondent by filing a written objection. In the meantime the respondent No. 1 as defendant No. 1 unsuccessfully filed an application for resection of plaint under order vii Rule 11 C.P.C. The learned Joint District Judge, Dhaka by order dated 02.10.2007 rejected the application for temporary injunction.

7. Against the said order of rejection the plaintiff-petitioner filed Civil Revision No.302 of 2007 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned District Judge, Dhaka while admitting the revision on 17.10.2007 stayed the operation of the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Then on an application for correction filed by the plaintiff-petitioner the learned District Judge by the order dated 24-10-2007 stayed all further proceedings of the Title Execution case No. 45 of 1989 till disposal of the civil revision pending before him.

8. Being aggrieved by the order dated 24.10.2007 the present-respondent No. 1 preferred Civil Revision, No.838 of 2008 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule and upon hearing both the parties a Division Bench of the High Court Division by Judgment and order 17.04.2008 made the Rule absolute setting aside the order dated 24.10.2007. The petitioner being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 17.04.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No 383 of 2008 preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division.

<u>9. We have heard the submission of Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and also perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other materials on record. It appears that the High Court Division rightly found that exparte decree passed in favour of the defendant-respondent No.1 in Title Suit No.291 of 1985 was maintained up to the Appellate Division in Civil Appeal No.361 of 2002. So he should not be deprived of enjoying the benefit of the said decree. The High Court Division is of the views that if the proceeding of the execution case in question is somehow blocked either in the form of injunction or stay the decree which the defendant-respondent No.1 obtained on 26.04.1989 shall be made nugatory and that will definitely shake the faith and confidence of the litigant people in judicial system of the country. The High Court Division is also of the view that if the plaintiff petitioner has filed the suit for declaration of her title and if she is evicted there from in execution of the decree there would be no bar to make necessary amendment in the plaint incorporating the said fact of eviction and making a prayer for recovery of khas possession thereof. It appears that the High Court Division has rightly noticed that the learned District Judge did not assign any reason whatsoever in passing the impugned order and he also failed to consider the fact that the plaintiff-petitioner admitted the filing of the previous suit by him challenging the exparte decree and dismissal of the suit by the Appellate Division. The High Court Division rightly found that the learned District Judge combined error of law on an important question of law that when the decree obtained by a party is maintained by the highest court of the country and such decree cannot   be made ineffective or nugatory somehow. Thus the learned Judges of the High Court Division rightly found that the learned District Judge committed error, of law in exercising its jurisdiction under Sub, Section (2) of Section 115 of the Code and in that view of the mater they have not considered it proper to send the respondent again to the Court of District Judge when Sub-Section (4) of the said Section gave the respondent the right to move the High Court Division. On perusal of the materials on record and the impugned judgment and order passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division and having considered the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly made the Rule absolute on proper consideration of the materials on record.</u>

10. In view of the above findings and observation we do not find any merit in the leave petition.

11. Accordingly, the leave petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.670 of 2004
lawyer:
For Petitioners: Mr. Mahhubey Alam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record. 
For Respondent: Mr. Joynal Abedin, No.3 Advocate, instructed by Mr. Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record

parties:
Md. Mizanur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Versus

full_judgment:
Mr. Syed .J. R. Mudassir Husain, C.J:- This civil petition for leave to appeal, at the instance of plaintiff, is directed against the judgment and order dated 16-03-2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5242 of 2002 making the Rule absolute upon setting aside the order dated 27-07-2002 passed by the Joint District Judge in Title Suit No. 12 of 2002 staying all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.01 of 2002. 

2. The facts leading to this petition, are that one Md. Mohsin Khan, predecessor-in-interest of the defendant-respondent Nos.I-5 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.22 of 1994 on 27-04-1994 for partition; upon hearing the parties the said partition suit was decreed on 09-05-1996 against the defendant-respondent Nos. 143, 144 and 232 and ex-parte against the rest in preliminary form and after receipt of the report of the Advocate Commissioner effecting partition the said preliminary decree was made final on 25-07-2001 and thereupon the said plaintiff-respondents put the final decree in execution by filing Title Execution Case No.01 of 2002 for possession of the suit property. 

3. In the meantime. the leave-petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.I2 of 2002 on 16-06-2002 for setting aside the aforesaid final decree dated 25-07-2001 passed in the aforesaid Title Suit No,22 of 1994 along with order dated 04-06-2002 for requisition of the police force for giving delivery of possession of the property passed in the said Title Execution Case No.01 of 2002. His main case was that by two deeds dated 07-01-1997 and 03-03 I 997 he along with his two brothers purchased the entire share of Jalal Patwary the defendant-respondent No.234 and the same was allotted to him in the preliminary decree dated 09-05-1996. It has been further stated that the said Jalal Patwary died on 28-05-2000, but the preliminary decree was made final against him without bringing his legal representatives on record and as such the final decree being nullity the aforesaid execution case was liable to be dismissed. 

4. On 27-06-2002, the plaintiff-petitioner made an application under Section 15I read with Order 21 Rule 26 of the Code of Civil Procedure in his suit for stay of all further proceedings of the said Title Execution Case No.1 of 2002 mainly on the ground that final decree was drawn against dead person named, Jalal Patwary defendant-respondent No.234 being a nullity can not be executed. 

5. Md. Mohsin Khan, predecessor-in-interest of the defendant-respondents opposed the aforesaid application dated 27-06-2002 by filing counter affidavit and denied the material allegations made in the application. Upon hearing the parties the learned Joint District Judge stayed all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No.01 of 2002 by his order dated 27-06-2002 and challenging the aforesaid order, the respondents moved the High Court Division in revision and the learned Judges of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. Hence, this leave-petition by the petitioner as plaintiff of Title Suit No. 12 of 2002. 

6. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, contended that Jalal Patwary admittedly died during process of final decree which was within full knowledge of Md. Mohshin Khan, the plaintiff of the original Title Suit No.22 of 1994 having also knowledge of deposition of predecessor in interest of the deceased Jalal Patwary upon the petitioner No.1 and his two brothers with malafide intention did neither substitute the heirs of the deceased Jalal Patwary nor impleaded the petitioner and his two brothers in order to obtain fraudulent final decree and as such the High Court Division having totally misconceived erred in law in holding the view that the application of the petitioner No. 1 for stay made under Order 21 Rule 26 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Suit No, 12 of 2002 as not maintainable. Learned Counsel further contended that the High Court Division committed an error of law holding that the learned Joint District Judge acted in excess of jurisdiction in granting stay of all further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 1 of 2002 by filing the aforesaid Title Suit No. 12 of 2002. 

7. Mr. Joynal Abedin, the learned Counsel appearing for the respondents, supporting the impugned judgment of the High Court Division, contended that the High Court Division having considered the facts and circumstances of the case rightly found that the application of the petitioner for stay made under Order 21 Rule 26 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Title Suit No. 12 of 2002 is wholly misconceived and that under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure is equally not maintainable and the learned Joint District Judge acted in excess of his jurisdiction in granting stay in Title Suit No.12 of 2002 of all Further proceedings of Title Execution Case No, 1 of 2002 filed by the respondents. 

8. We have heard the learned lawyers of both sides and considered their submissions. It appears that the High Court Division having considered the facts and circumstances of the ease held as follows: 
"The facts which are not disputed are that Md. Moshin Khan on 09-05-1996 got the preliminary decree on contest against defendant Nos. 143, 144 and 232. By purchasing by two deeds dated 07-01-1997 and 03-03-1997, opposite party No.1 Mizanur Rahman and his two brothers acquired the entire share of said defendant No,232, which was allotted to him in the aforesaid preliminary decree, The purchasers thereby entered into the shoos of deceased defendant No.232. 

Meanwhile, said Mohsin Khan took steps for partition and the Advocate Commissioner appointed submitted his report effecting partition of the suit land. The Court accepted the report in due course and mad eth preliminary decree final on 25-07-2001. Said Mohsin then put the decree into execution in aforesaid Title Execution Case No.1 of 2002 for possession of his share. Opposite party No.1 however preferred not to take any step either for his substitution or addition in place of said decreed Jalal Patwary in the suit. He also did not raise any objection to the execution of the decree before the executing Court. 

Instead, as stated above opposite party No. 1 instituted Title Suit No, 12 of 2002 against the petitioners and others for setting aside the final decree and all orders passed in the execution case. 

Opposite party No. 1 claims that defendant No.232 Jalal Patwary died on 28-05-2000 before the preliminary decree was made final on 25-07-2001. In support, he has produced a copy of a death certificate issued on behalf of a hospital. On the other hand, petitioner claims that said Jalal Patwary died on 29-07-2001 after the preliminary decree was made final. They also produced a certificate from the local Chairman to that effect. Date of death of defendant No.232 Jalal Patwary has therefore become a highly contested question of fact which cannot be decided here in this revisional proceeding." 

The High Court Division further held as follows: 

"What surprised us most is if opposite parity No.1 was so sure that their predecessor-in-interest defendant No.232 Jalal Patwary died on 28-05-2000 then why he did no take any step thereto in Title Suit No.22 of 1994 and why he allowed the preliminary decree to be made final against said deceased Jalal Patwary. In 1997, he purchased the entire share of said Jalal Patwary that was allotted to him in the preliminary decree. So, he could not claim that he was not aware of said decree. In the fitness of things, most natural and proper step for said opposite party No.1 was to take step for substitution or addition in place of deceased defendant No.232 Jalal Patwary in the suit. 

Instead, on 16-06-2002 opposite party No. 1 instituted Title Suit No. 12 of 2002 for setting aside the final decree on the ground of nullity. Even in 2002 opposite party No, 1 could have achieved very same objective by taking step before the executing Court which is the only forum to decide whether the decree was still valid for execution; But he has not taken any step before the executing Court challenging the final decree till date". 

9. In view of the above findings, the learned Advocate for the petitioner finds difficulty to pin point any error of law committed by the High Court Division, resulting in an error in the decision causing failure of justice. We, therefore, view that the High Court Division has rightly decided the case and there is no cogent ground for our interference. Accordingly, this petition is dismissed. 

End.
