case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 30.06.2009 passed by this Division in Civil Appeal Nos.08 and 09 of 2005)
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. Both the civil review petitions arise out the judgment and order dated 30.06.2009 passed by this Division in Civil Appeal Nos.08 and 09 or 2005 allowing the appeals setting aside the judgment and order dated 28.01.2002 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal Nos.203 and 108 of 1995 dismissing the appeals and affirming the judgment and decree dated 16.02.1995 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Gazipur in Title Suit Nos.16 and 17 of 1992 dismissing the suits.

2. The facts leading to the filing or civil petition for review No. 156 of 2009, in short, are that the respondents Mohiuddin Khan and another as the plaintiffs tiled the above Title Suit No. 16 of 1992 on 06.02.1992 against the heirs of Shihamul Haque (since deceased). Their case, in short, is that they by deeds of sale dated 01.02.1974, 15.02.1974, 11.02.1974 and 14.02.1974 respectively purchased .54 acre of land appertaining to C.S. No. 248 of C.S. khatian No. 235 corresponding to S.A. khatian No. 406 of mouza Chandana P.S. Joydebpur, District- Gazipur described in schedule 'A' to the plaint from Chaturi Tend and got delivery of possession. By Mutation Case No. 170/74-75 their names were mutated in S.A. Khatian No. 406 in place of said Chaturi Tanti and they paid ground rents and got dakhilas. Against the above order of mutation, Shihamul Haque preferred Miscellaneous Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 claiming title on the basis of deed of exchange (settlement) dated 16.06.1980 and the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, by the order dated 12.01.1982 cancelled the mutation. The appellants then filed Appeal No. 8 of 1982 and the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka who heard the appeal, having found that the respondents and others were in possession of the case land, set aside the order dated 12.01.1982 restoring the mutation in the names of respondents and others. Then Shihamul Haque preferred Appeal No. 96 of 1984 before the Board of Land Administration and after hearing the same was dismissed. Shihamul Haque then filed Writ Petition No. 159 of 1989 before the high Court Division. The High Court Division declared the above orders by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka and the Board of Land Administration 'to have been passed without any lawful authority with the observation that the question of title and ownership and validity of the deeds in question could be gone into and decided only by a civil court. The respondents from the proceedings of the above Miscellaneous Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 and also from the contents of the annexure of the above Writ Petition No. 159 of 1989 for the first time came to know about the alleged deed of agreement for exchange dated 30.10.1963, the alleged powers of attorneys dated 07.06.1965, the deed of exchange dated 16.06.1980 in terms of Exchange Case No. 35/69-70, Title Suit Nos.27 of 1971 and 150 of 1972, Civil Revision Nos.315 and 1387 of 1977. The respondents are bonafide purchasers of the suit land for valuable consideration without any notice of the agreement of exchange and other facts as stated above. Ordinance No. 1 of 1964 (E.P. Disturbed Persons Rehabilitation Ordinance, 1964) having died by the efflux of time on 31.12.1964 as held in the case of Chaitta Ranjan Sutar Vs. Secretary, Judicial Department and others 17 DLR 451, the above proceeding of Exchange Case No. 35/69-70 started on 24.07.1969 for forfeiting the land of thy respondents for the purpose of granting the so-called settlement was without jurisdiction. Possession of the property in question was always with the respondent, and was never taken over by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka or the then Sub-Divisional Officer and the same were never enlisted in the Census List of 1966-1967.

3. The defendants-petitioners contested the above suit by filing written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that Shihamul Haque, his father Anamul Haq and mother Tahera Sogra Begum, were the inhabitants of Bardwan district in India. After they settled in the then East Pakistan in 1950 migrating from India, Chaturi Tanti along with Shibulal, Buttu, Surjagaya and Nathan "Fanti proposed to exchange their lands including suit land of the above mouza Chandana with the land of Shamsul Hoque, Enamul Hoque and Tahera Sogra Begum at Bardwan. Accordingly, a deed of agreement was duly executed which was registered on 30.10.1963 and pursuant to the above agreement the parties handed over possession of their respective lands to each other acknowledging delivery of possession. Embargo having been created upon the Hindus to transfer their properties by registered deed of conveyances on promulgation of Defence of Pakistan Rules, several powers of attorney were given to each other by either the sides on the basis or which deeds of exchange were executed in Bardawan in India. By one of such deeds of exchange dated 09.08.1968 executed in India Tahera Sogra Begun exchanged 1.36 acres of her lands at Bardwan with .89 acre land of Chaturi and Nathuni Tanti of mouza Chandana including the suit land. Bhatu Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and 3 others made joint declaration before the Notary Public in Calcutta on 15.07.1968 and 12.08.1968 confirming the above exchange of their lands of mouza Chandana including the suit land. The facts of the execution and registration of the above agreement to exchange in the year 1963, the irrevocable power of attorney and the exchange deeds were duly certified by the Magistrate,. First Class, Alipur, West Bengal, India on 17.07.1968 and 10.09.1968. Shihamul Haque applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka praying for permission to execute and register the deed of exchange under the authority of the general power of attorney executed in his favour whereupon Exchange Case No. 35/69-70 was started. Shibulal Tanti, Chaturi Tanti and others filed an objection in the above exchange case contending, inter-alia, they did not enter into any such agreement nor did they exchange their properties. They further contended that the deed of exchange is fraudulent and powers of attorney are collusive and were vitiated by coercion, threat and intimidation. Shibulal Tanti also filed Title Suit No. 27 of 1971 in the 1st Court' of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Shihamul Haque and others challenging the deed of egret:- Mont for exchange, powers of attorney as well as the deed of exchange but the suit was dismissed for non-prosecution. Subsequently he prayed for restoration of the suit which was rejected by the order dated 08.06.1972. After that Shibulal Tanti filed Title Suit No. 150 of 1972 in the same court against Shihamul Haque and others seeking same declarations as made in the previous suit and then prayed for amendment which was rejected as the suit filed earlier was dismissed. Against the order of rejection, Shibulal Tanti filed Civil Revision No. 315 of 1977 and Civil Revision No. 1372 of 1977 on more or less similar grounds. Then both the above Rules were discharged on the basis of prayers of Shibulal Tanti to the effect that they did not want to press the Rules. Alter disposal of the above suits/revisions Shihamul Haque applied to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka to proceed with the Exchange Case No. 35 of 1969-70. After snaking necessary enquiry and completing all the formalities the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka executed and registered the deed of exchange (Settlement) on 16.06.1980 transferring 7.12 acres of land of mouza Chandana in favour of Shihamul Haque. Soon after on the basis of the above deed of exchange Shihamul Haque started Mutation Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 in the office of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, praying for canceling the earlier mutation in the name of the plaintiffs-respondents and got the mutation cancelled. Against the order of cancellation, the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka in Appeal Case No. 8 of 1982 set aside the order of the Additional Deputy commissioner (Dhaka). Shihamul Haque moved the Board of Land Administration and having been unsuccessful filed Writ Petition No. 154 of 1989 in which the Rule was made absolute with the observation that the question of title and validity of the, deed of exchange could be decided only by the civil court. The defendants have been possessing the suit land along with other lands by cultivating and growing crops therein through bargadars, namely, Kamal's mother and her son-in-law.

4. The respondents in Civil Review Petition No. 56 of 2009, i.e Sree Monmohan Shaha and another as the plaintiffs on 25.02.1992 filed Title Suit No. 25 of 1992 against the heirs of Shihamul Haque and others claiming similar reliefs on more or less similar averments made in Title Suit No. 16 of 1992, variation being that the area of the suit land was .98 acre as described in schedules A, B and C to the plaint. Respondent No.  1 purchased from Shibulal Tanti 0.02 acre of land of Plot No. 1952 of Khatian No. 68, 0.35 acre of land of Plot No. 1905 of Khatian No. 290, .05 acre of land of Plot No. 1916 of Khatian No. 429 all within the said mouza Chandana by registered deeds of sale dated 24.01.1979. Plaintiff-respondent No. 2 also purchased .06 acre of land of the aforesaid Plot No. 1916 and some other land from aforesaid Plot No. 1952 by registered deed of sale dated 06.01.1979 from the aforesaid Shibulal Tanti and they were put into possession of the suit land immediately. They had filed Separation and Mutation Case No. 1384 of 1978-79 in the office of Circle Officer (Revenue), Joydebpur and their names were mutated in S.A. Khatian Nos.68, 290 and 429 under the order of Circle Officer. (Revenue) dated 19.06.1979 and they have been paying ground rent for the suit land since 06.09.1979. The plaint of the above suit also contained averments regarding filing of Miscellaneous Appeal Case No. 13 of 1981 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, Appeal No. 8 of 1982 before Additional Commissioner, Appeal No. 96 of 1984 before Board of Land Administration and Writ Petition No. 159 of 1989 before the High Court Division. In the above suit defendant Nos.1(a)-1(d), the heirs of Shihamul Haque also filed written statement making averments similar to their written statement filed in Title Shit No. 16 of 1992.

5. The trial Court by judgment and order dated 16.02.1995 dismissed both Title Suit Nos.16 and 25 of 1992 against which, the respondents preferred first Appeal Nos.108 and 203 of 1995 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 28.01.2002 dismissed both the appeals.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with judgment and decree of the High Court Division, the leave respondents filed both the Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal before this Division. This Division granted leave in both the civil petitions. Accordingly, Civil Appeal Nos. 08 and 09 of 2005 have been initiated.

7. This Division upon hearing the parties by its judgment and order dated 30.06.2009 allowed both the appeals setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the High Court Division and decreed both the suits.

8. Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by this Division in the above appeals, the review petitioners filed both the review petitions before this Division.

9. Mr. Ajmalul Hossain, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the review petitioners in both the petitions, submits that this Division committed a mistake or an error in holding that the respondents are bonafide purchasers and that it is clear from the records that they were well aware of the fact that the title of the suit land is disputed and that litigation was going on between the predecessors- in-interest of the respondents and the petitioners. He further submits that this Division committed mistake or an error of law and fact in holding that the possession has been with the respondents on the basis of an alleged admission in the pleading although it is apparent from the evidence that the possession has been with the petitioners throughout and that the Court of Subordinate Judge and the High Court Division also found possession of the petitioners. He also submits that this Division by its judgment and order dated 30.06.2009 committed a mistake or an nor in law in giving relief in respect of a deed of settlement transferring 7.12 acres of land whereas the plaintiffs-respondents in the title suits claimed .98 acre in schedule-A, B, C, in Title Suit N9.25 of 1992 and .54 acre in Schedule-A in Title Suit No.  161 of 1992 respectively.

10. Mr. Mahmudul Islam learned Senior Advocate for the respondents, however, supports the impugned judgment.

<u>11. We have considered the submissions of both the learned Advocates, the impugned judgment and the materials on record. This Division came to a finding that sections 4,6 and 6A were declared ultravires the Constitution in the case of Chitta Ranjan Sutar (ibid) and therefore the position is that Sections 4, 6 and 6A never existed before. Moreover, Ordinance of 1964 died a natural death by the efflux of time and the Exchange Case No. 35 of 1969-70 having been started on 24.07.1969 for forfeiting the land and for settlement has been taken without any lawful authority.</u>

12. Mr. Willoughby was quoted in the case of Abdul Majid Vs. Kashem Ali (1975) 27 DLR 1 to explain the position of an unconstitutional law which runs as under:-

"An unconstitutional act is not a law, it confers no right, it imposes no duties, it offers no protection, it creates no office; it is in legal contemplation, as inoperative as though it had never been passed."

13. It appears that the deed of settlement of the petitioners was issued under the authority of Act XLV of 1974 and not under Ordinance No.  I of 1964. Moreover D.W.1 in her deposition in no uncertain terms admitted “বিনিময় মোঃ ৩৫/৬৯-৭০ তে ২০-১১-৭০ ইং তারিখে জেলা প্রশাসক এর দেয় নোটিশে উল্লেখিত, সম্পত্তি বাজেয়াপ্রাপ্তকৃত সম্পত্তি নয়।”

14. Therefore, it appears that the Government did not have any authority to forfeit the land under Section 6A of the Ordinance No.  I of 1964 and in fact it did not forfeit the land under Ordinance No.  I of 1964. There is nothing on record that the property was enemy property or vested property and therefore the Government did not have any authority to grant settlement of the land in question in favour of the defendants-petitioners.

15. Having considered the evidence of the witnesses this Division found that the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land. In paragraph 45 of the written statement, the petitioners admitted that they were dispossessed by the respondents from the homestead land and the exchange lands during pendency of the exchange proceeding. In addition to above, in paragraph-55 of the written statement the petitioners admitted that they were dispossessed in August 1972. This Division further hold that the plaintiff’s respondents sufficiently proved their possession in the suit land and that the defendants were admittedly out of possession and that therefore the findings of the High Court Division and the trial Court on this point were not tenable in law.

<u>16. Admittedly the plaintiffs-respondents arc bonafide purchasers for value without notice of the deed of exchange of the petitioners. According to Section-3 of Transfer of Property Act an unregistered deed of exchange cannot amount to a notice and as such the interest of the respondents as bonafide purchasers of the suit land for valuable consideration without notice of the agreement of exchange is protected. In the case in hand, there is a contest between two valid documents of which one is registered and the other is not. Since the respondents could prove that they are bonafide purchasers for valuable consideration without notice of the unregistered deed of exchange of the petitioners, their right cannot be taken away.</u>

17. What is important to note here is that the deed of the petitioners covers an area of 7.12 acres of land whereas the respondents claimed .98 acres of land in Title Suit No. 25 of 1992 and .54 acre of land in Title Suit No. 16 of 1994. Therefore, in all fairness, findings of this Court should apply in respect of 1.52 acres of land described in the schedules of both the suits. The judgment delivered by this Division in Civil Appeal Nos.8 and 9 of 1925 shall be limited only to 1.52 acres of land not the rest of the land covered by the deed of settlement of the petitioners.

18. In the light of findings made before, it appears that the petitioners could not make out any case for reviewing (hi impugned judgment warranting interference by this Division.

19. Therefore, we do not find any substance in the review petitions. Accordingly, the Civil Review Petitions are dismissed with the observations made in the body of the judgment.

End.

caseno: Civil Appeal No. 140 of 2008
lawyer:
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, Senior Advocate instructed by Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Appellate 
Faruque Ahmed, Senior Advocate instructed by Md. Abdul Hai, Advocate-on-Record -------- For the Respondents
parties:
Rabeya Khatun and others ------- Appellants
VS
Monowara Begum and others -------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 24th day of May, 2006 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3971 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 24th day of May, 2006 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.3971 of 1998 making the Rule absolute.

<u>2. Facts necessary for disposal of this appeal are that the predecessors in-interest of respondent Nos. 1-17 as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 164 of 1991 in the Court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title in the suit land and also for a declaration that sale deed being No. 8310 dated 09.09.1956 was forged, fraudulent and inoperative on the averment that the suit land along with other lands appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 62 originally belonged to Saddat Bepari who died before the S.A. operation leaving behind his wife, Shamchun Nessa, one son named Shamsul Haque and two daughters named Hajera Khatun and Saleha Khatun as his heirs. Before death, Saddat Bepari transferred the suit land along with other lands in favour of his legal heirs by an oral gift and they were possessing the suit land. During the S.A. operation, the suit land measuring 1.70 acres appertaining to S.A. Plot No. 198 was recorded in the name of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs have been paying rents regularly and possessing the land in ejmali, From the local Tashil Office, the plaintiffs learned that the defendants got their names mutated in the record on the basis of sale deed dated 19.09.1956 purportedly executed and registered by them in favour of one Hazi Abdul Aziz. The plaintiffs filed Miscellaneous Case No. 230 of 1989-90 before the Assistant Commissioner (Land) for mutation of their names. The case is pending since the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land was clouded because of the deed dated,19.09.1956 created by the defendants and the subsequent deeds on the basis of the said deed, the plaintiffs were compelled to file the suit for the relief aforementioned.</u>

3. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs acquired .89 acre land appertaining to Suit Plot No.198 and other two plots on the basis of a decree passed in Partition Suit No.5 of 1951. Thereafter, the plaintiffs as the owners it possession of the suit land sold the same to Haji Abdul Aziz by kabala dated 19.09.1956 and delivered possession of the transferred land to him and he possessed the same. Abdul Aziz being in Possession of the suit land for more than 12 years sold the same to one Abu Taib Abu in the early part of 1970. Abu Taib wanted to purchase the land in the name of his wife, Gulenur, but as the writer had lost the sale deed dated 19.05.1956 of Haji Aziz, he could not execute the kabala in favour of Gulenur. Abu Taib alias Abu had possessed the suit land in favour of his wife and he died in 1975. Subsequently, Abdul Aziz transferred 84 acre land appertaining to S.A. Plot No. 198 to Gulenur Bibi by two sale deeds dated 27.10.1981 being deed Nos. 26232 and 26185. Gulenur Bibi transferred 84 acre land in favour of defendant Nos. 2-8 by two registered Heba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 16.09.1985 being deed Nos. 1601 and 1652 and delivered possession of the transferred land to them and the defendants are in possession thereof by virtue of the said heba deeds and they mutated their names. As the price of the land has gone up because of the construction of Dhaka Protection Embankment, the plaintiffs filed the suit.

4. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 29.04.1993 dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 167 of 1993 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge (now the Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Dhaka, hearing the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 22.04.1998 dismissed the appeal. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiffs   preferred Civil Revision No. 3971 of 1998 before the High Court Division and a learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the judgments and decrees of the Courts below, but did not say anything about the fate of the suit. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 47 of 2007 before this Court and leave was granted on 08.08.2008 to consider the submissions   made by their learned Advocate to the following effect:

"The learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners submits that the plaintiffs having been able to seek further relief by way of partition and recovery of Khas possession than a mere declaration of title, omitted to do so, the suit is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, which the High Court Division failed to consider and thereby committed serious error of 1 law in reversing the concurrent decision of the courts below, resulting in failure of justice."

<u>5. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Counsel, appearing for the appellants, has submitted that both the Courts below concurrently found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land, the suit for mere declaration of title without the prayer for consequential relief as provided in the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act was not maintainable in law, but the High Court Division failed to consider the proviso to section 42 of the Act and vis-a-vis the finding of possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs and thus erred in law in making the Rule absolute. He has further submitted that the High Court Division did not at all consider the oral evidence as regards the possession of the suit land and did not also reverse the finding of the Courts below in that regard and it simply stated that "It appears that the evidence led by the plaintiffs on the point of possession is slightly better to find the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs and on such finding interfered with the concurrent finding of fact that the plaintiffs failed to prove their possession in the suit land and as such, the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable in law and the same be set aside and the appeal be allowed.</u>

6. Mr. Faruque Ahmed, learned Counsel, for the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order.

7. From the judgment of the trial Court, it appears that it gave the finding, inter alia, that the plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land. In coming to the said finding, the trial Court considered the evidence of PW1 (PW1 was plaintiff No. 9) who stated in his cross-examination that they never possessed the suit land and he could not say the chauhaddi of the suit land; PW1 further stated that they did not possess the suit land for the last 30/36 years and none possess the suit land. The trial Court considered the testimony of PW2 in his cross-examination that neither the plaintiffs nor the defendants possessed the suit land and that 2/2½ years before, the defendants erected a 'Ghar' on the suit land and those of PW3 in his examination-in-chief that the suit land was under water. It further appears that the trial Court gave further finding that the defendants failed to prove their possession too. The trial Court rightly opined that the defendants' weakness, if any, would not entitle the plaintiffs to get the decree in the suit. The Appellate Court being the last Court of fact also concurred with the said finding of the trial Court on detailed consideration of the evidence, oral and documentary. But, unfortunately, the High Court Division without referring to any evidence, whatsoever, in a very casual manner found title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the finding that "It appears that the evidence led by the plaintiffs on the point of possession is slightly better to find the possession of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs. On misconstruction of the evidence on record, the Courts below came to wrong finding of possession that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession. Further when the evidence on possession adducing by both the parties are evenly balanced the Courts below were required in law to find possession with the plaintiffs for the reason that the plaintiffs succeeded in proving their title. In other words, when the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title in the suit land, the plaintiffs should be taken to have discharged their onus to prove possession on the basis of evidence on record,"

<u>8. As regards the sale deed dated 19.09.1956, the trial Court found that although the plaintiffs claimed that the said kabala was fraudulent and collusive, they did not examine any witness to prove the said fact and the plaintiffs also failed to examine any witness to prove as to how forgery was committed in creating the said deed. The Appellate Court observed that since the plaintiffs claimed that the kabala dated 19.09.1956 was forged, the onus was upon them to prove the same as forged. The Appellate Court further observed that the kabala was a registered one and was 40 years old and in law, it had a presumption of correctness and thus it endorsed the view of the trial Court. We find nothing wrong with the view taken by the Courts below. In this regard, the High Court Division made a total wrong approach in observing that since PW1 deposed on his behalf and on behalf of the other plaintiffs that the alleged sale deed was forged and fraudulent as neither his sister nor he himself ever went to the office of Sub-Registrar and executed and registered the same, the onus was discharged by the plaintiffs that the deed in question was forged and fraudulent. And in the context, the learned Judge totally misconceived the provisions of section 103 of the Evidence Act.</u>

<u>9. It is by now a well settled legal principle that when the Courts below concur on a question of fact (possession is surely a question of fact), the High Court Division exercising jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure can interfere only when such finding is either based on misreading or on non-consideration of the material evidence, but the High Court Division except making a general observation as quoted hereinbefore failed to point out either any misreading or non-consideration of any material evidence. Therefore, it erred in law in interfering with the decisions of the Courts below which dismissed the suit. Further in view of the clear admission of PW1 in his cross-examination (he was plaintiff No. 9 in the suit) that they had not been in possession in the suit land for the last 30/36 years, the plaintiffs' suit for declaration of title without the prayer, consequential relief was not maintainable in law in view of the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act.</u>

10. For the discussions made above, we find merit in the appeal and accordingly, the same is allowed. The impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is set aside and those of the Courts below are restored, However, there will be no order as to cost.

End.

Vs.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 13th January, 2009 passed by the High Cowl Division in Civil Revision No.2987 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 13.01.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2987 of 2004 making the Rule absolute and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 06.04.2004 passed by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No. 39 of 2003 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 10.03.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 102 of 1999 dismissing the suit.

<u>2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the petitioner-plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 102 of 1999 before the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj seeking declaration of title, confirmation of possession and recovery of khas possession in the suit land measuring an area of 21 decimals as shown in the 'Ka' schedule land to the plaint and also to the structures as shown in the "Kha" and "Ga" schedule land to the plaint appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 189 and S.A. Khatian No. 47, Poura Fielding No. 210/1, Bangabandhu Sarak, Police Station Narayangonj Sadar. The plaintiff contended, inter alia, that Harun Bepari was the, owner and possessor of the said land and accordingly it was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 48 in his name; that said Damn Bepari published a public notice in the daily Ittefaq dated 07.01.1978 forming the said land. Thereafter, the plaintiff purchased the said land by sub-kabala deed dated 23.01.1978 and acquired title in the "Ka" schedule land to the plaint, filled up the land with earth, constructed some structures upon the said land and let out the same to his sister, the defendant No. 3 and started possessing the suit land and structure through tenants and also by himself. A dispute arose between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 in respect of title of the suit land and the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 174 of 1981. That suit was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 12.05.1983. Thereafter, the plaintiff purchased the suit land again from the defendants No. 4 and 5 by two registered kabala deeds dated 06.06.1983 and 21.06.1983. The defendant No. 3 entered into a portion of the suit premises on 01.07.1978 by executing an agreement and thereafter he refused to pay rent whereupon the plaintiff instituted SCC Suit No. 28 of 1984 for evicting the defendant No. 3. The plaintiff in the instant suit prayed for declaration of title to the "Ka" schedule land to the plaint and confirmation of possession of the "Kha" schedule structure on the suit land and recovery of khas possession to "Ga" schedule structure on the suit land.</u>

3. The defendant No. 2, Narayangonj Jila Parishad contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable as it stands framed. It was claimed that 12 decimals of land out of the suit land was acquired by the Government vide LA. Case No.  of 1935-36 and thereafter .054 acre of land was acquired for the development   of Dhaka-Narayangonj Road. Thereafter, the land was leased out by defendant No. 2 to defendant No. 3 who is in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff previously instituted two suits against the defendants, and having lost those has filed the instant suit. The plaintiff has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and there was no cause of action to file the suit and the suit was not maintanable in its present form and manner. Hence, the suit was liable to be dismissed.

<u>4. The trial Court upon consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 10.03.2003 holding the suit to be barred by res judicata.</u>

5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and, decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 39 of 2003. The said appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj, who by the judgment and decree dated 06.04.2004 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

6. The defendant filed a civil revisional application before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and set aside the judgment and decrees dated 06.04.2004 passed by the appellate Court thereby restored the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Hence, the plaintiff petitioner herein has filed the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division.

7. Mr. Muhammad Nawab Ali, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the High Court Division erred in reversing the reasoned judgment of the appellate Court. He further submits that the High Court Division did not consider the fact that L.A. Case No.  of 1935-36 acquired only 08 acres of land which was confirmed by local investigation report. As such the High Court Division erred in not decreeing the remainder of the suit land in favour of the petitioner. He lastly submits that the dismissal of the entire suit was therefore illegal and the judgment and order of the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.

8. Mrs. Sufia Khatun, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate-on-Record for the parties concerned and perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

<u>10. We note from the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division that observation was made to the effect that the earlier Title Suit No. 174 of 1981 (marked as -Ext."Ka" in the suit) was also filed seeking a declaration of title in the suit land and structures raised upon holding No. 210/1 of Narayangonj Municipality, Plot No.  28/961 corresponding to schedule-`Ka', `Kha' and 'Ga' land of the plaint. It was further observed that the plaintiff of the earlier suit is the plaintiff of the instant suit. In the earlier suit the Zilla Board Narayangonj as defendant produced the; order sheets of the aforementioned L.A. case marked as Exts. 'A', 'B' and 'C' and gazette notification was marked as Ext. D. The trial Court in that suit came to a denied finding that the original owner received compensation in the said L.A. ease and declared that no title passed in favour of the plaintiff on the strength of kobala deed dated 23.01.1978. No appeal was preferred against the dismissal of the said suit. The High Court Division also observed that the instant suit was filed on the strength of two subsequent kobala deeds dated 06.06.1983 and 21.06.1983 (Exts. 11 and 12) from Nazimuddin, son of late Abdul Gafur alleging the executants to be the grandson of Harun Bepari. The High Court Division observed that the compensation in L.A. Case No.  of 1935-36 was in the name of two sons of Harm Bepari, namely Sirajuddin and Tafizuddin and that fact was affirmed in the earlier title suit and therefore the plaintiff could not make out a case of alleged purchase from the heirs of Harun Bepari. The High Court Division observed that so long Ext. 'Ka' stands, the plaintiff is estopped from claiming any title in the suit land through the heirs of Harun Bepari inasmuch as in the previously instituted suit, the Court believed payment of compensation to the sons of Harun Bepari.</u>

<u>11. As the suit land is common in both Title Suit No. 174 of 1981 as well as in the instant suit and the plaintiff claimed title through the heirs of Harun Bepari and since the earlier suit was dismissed on contest and the issue relating to right, title and possession is the same, the instant suit is clearly barred by the doctrine of a res judicata.</u>

12. The high Court Division has given elaborate reasons for making the Rule absolute thereby upholding the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

13. We do not find any cause to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

14. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1631 of 2009
lawyer:

case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 18.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 820 of 1997)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Matin J.:- This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 18.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 820 of 1997 against the judgment and decree dated 30.10.1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Court No. 2, Jessore in Title Appeal No. 239 of 1987 reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.08.1987 passed by the Monirampur Upazila Munsif Adalat, Monirampur, Jessore in Title Suit No. 228 of 1984. 

2. The facts, in short, are that the respondents-opposite party respondent Nos.1-3 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 228 of 1984 in the court of the Monirampur Upazila Munsif Adalat; Monirampur, Jessore impleading the predecessor of the petitioners and other respondents as defendants for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and khas possession in respect of the suit property. 

3. The plaintiffs in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 228 of 1984 stated in the pliant that the suit land measuring 35 decimals of land in plot Nos. 170, 176 and 178 of mouza baliadanga of Monirampur Police Staticin, District-Jessore belonged to C.S. recorded tenant Arjun Muchi and others and one Dakhu Rani was his upper landlord and subsequently one Kashinath purchased her rent receiving interest and took the land as his khas property and thereby S.A. record has been prepared in his name. The plaintiffs further stated that practically Kashinath did not get possession but Arjun Muchi possessed the suit land and resided therein by creating house till his death-and his only son the plaintiff Panchu Gopal Das has been possessing the same. Due to preparation of S.A. record in the name of Kashinath to avoid complexity of law, the plaintiff Panchu Gopal on 22.02.1979 obtained a registered kabala deed from Kashinath and the plaintiff had lawful title over the suit land. The plaintiff further stated that on 15.02.1982 the ADC (Revenue), Jessore passed an illegal order regarding correction of S.A. record and on the basis of that order defendant No.1 threatened the plaintiff with dispossession and accordingly the plaintiff filed the present suit. 

4. The predecessor of the present petitioners and pro-forma-respondent Nos. 8 and 9 of the present civil .petition for leave to appeal as defendant Nos. 1,6 and 7 in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 228 of 1984 con-tested the suit on filing. a joint written statement stating therein in the written statement denying all the material allegation made in the plaint and contended, inter-alia, that the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable in it's present form and manner and the same is barred by limitation and the suit. land originally belonged to C.S. recorded tenants, Kashinath and others and thereafter due to arrear of rents the suit land including other undisputed land was sold in auction and the Government purchased the suit land in auction sale vide certificate case No. 135 of 1955-56 and thereby the Government went into possession of the suit land including other undisputed land which during S.A. operation was wrongly recorded in the name of Panchu Rishhi and others and for that the Tahsildcr, Gopalpur of Monirampur Police Station filed objection Case No. 52 of 1956 under Section 19(1) of the 1.B.S.A. and T. Act against the said wrong preparation of S.A. record and that Objection case on proper hearing of both sides was allowed and aforesaid initial S.A. record of Panchu Muchi @ Rishi and others was cancelled and title and possession of the Government to the suit land was established on due cancellation of wrong S.A. Kh.125 of the suit land. Thus when the Government was in peaceful possession with the title as stated above in the suit land and other undisputed land on due inclusion of the same in the Government's S.A. khatian No. 1 settled 24 decimals of land from disputed plot No. 170 with an area of 12 decimals, Plot No. 178 with a area of 02 decimals and undisputed plot No.188/698 with an area of 10 decimals to the defendant No. 1 vide settlement case No. 29/XIII/61-62 on 30.06.1961 on due realisation of salami from the settlement holder, the defendant No. 1 on 07.08.1961 and thereby the defendant No. 1 on the strength of the aforesaid settlement has mutated his name for the said land on regular payment of tent to the Government and the Government has also executed a registered kabuliyat on 02.01.1979 for the said 24 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No. 1. After registration of the aforesaid kabuliyat the plaintiff has created the so-called collusive kobala dated 22.02.1979 and when the plaintiff on the basis of the said deed dated 22.02.1979 threatened the defendant No. 1 to dispossess him from the suit land the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 400 of 1983 wherein the defendant No. 1 obtained injunction against the plaintiff and the said title suit is still pending in the Monirarnpur Upazila Munsif Adalat. The defendant Nos. 1, 6 and 7 took eksonsa lease from the Government' for 04 decimals in. Plot No. 170, 08 decimals in Plot N0.176 and 04 decimals in Plot No.178 respectively and the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 arc residing therein by constructing katcha dwelling houses. S.A. record in S.A. Khatian No. 5 is wrong and S.A. Khatian 125 will be cancelled of the mouza concerned and the note is therein the 'working volume' of S.A. record also stands alike. So plaintiffs case is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

5. The Monirampur Upazila Munsif Adalat, Monirampur, Jessore on due consideration and assessment of 3(three) Ws. and 3 (three) I). Ws. and documents submitted by both the parties in the judgment and decree dated 30.08.1987 in Title Suit No. 228 of 1984 decreed in part for 21 decimals of land out of total disputed land of 35 decimals in favour of the plaintiff and title and possession of the defendant No. 1 over 14 decimals of land in disputed plot Nos. 170 and 178 on the basis of aforesaid settlement from Government is affirmed in the said judgment and decree dated 30.08.1987. 

6. 'Thereafter the predecessor of the present petitioners along with his two full brothers, the present proforma-respondent Nos. 8 and 9 who were defendant Nos. 1, 6 and 7 in the Title Suit No. 228 of 1984 being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 30.08.1987 preferred Title Appeal No. 239 of 1987 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Jessore and in that appeal the plaintiff-respondent Nos. 1-3 filed memorandum of cross objection on their behalf and finally on transfer the Title Appeal No. 239 of 1987 was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, Court No. 2, Jessore who in his judgment and decree dated 30.10.1996 dismissed the appeal and decreed the suit in full and also granted recovery of khas possession by evicting katcha huts of defendant Nos. 1, 6 and 7. 

7. As against the judgment of the appellate court the petitioner preferred civil revision before the High Court Division and by the impugned judgment the High Court Division discharged the Rule and affirmed the judgment of the court of appeal below. 

8. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the High Court Division the petitioners have preferred this petition for leave to appeal. 

9. Heard Dr. Kai Akter Hamid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners and perused the petition and the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other papers on record. 

10. It appears that the plaintiff proved that document dated 22.02.1979 which is a registered document from Kashi Nath. The plaintiff constructed dwelling huts thereon and the defendant forcibly constructed a kacca but in the eastern side of plot No. 178 and therefore the appellate court rightly gave the complete relief by allowing recovery of possession. 

11. The defendant adduced 3 D. Ws. and D.Ws.2 and 3 admitted the title and possession of the plaintiff and hence we find no illegality committed by the courts below in finding possession and title in favour of the plaintiff respondent. 

12. Accordingly the leave petition is dismissed. 

End.

caseno: Civil Appeal No. 45 of 2004
lawyer:
Mohammad Nazrul Islam, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Mudhu Malati Chowdhury Barua, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Appellant 
For the Respondents ------ Ex-parte
parties:
Kashaituli Jame Mosque Waqf ------ Appellant
VS
Md. Abdus Salam Bepari and others ------- Respondent
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 23rd day of April 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1998 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal by leave is from the judgment and order dated the 23rd day of April, 2002 passed by a learned judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1998 of 1998 Making the rule absolute.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of the appeal are that respondent No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.06 of 1984 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for partition of ejmali properties. Subsequently, the suit was transferred to the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge, 6 Dhaka and was remembered as Title Suit No. 289 of 1985. The appellant filed an application in the suit to add it as a defendant and it was added as defendant No.7. After being added as defendant No.7, it filed written statement to contest the suit. Then the suit was transferred to the Court of subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2 Dhaka, where it was renumbered as Title Suit No. 257 of 1990. The suit was again transferred to the Court of 4 Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 306 of 1990. The suit was decreed exparte on 03.05.1992 and the decree was drawn up on 05.10.1992.

3. The defendant appellant filed and application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) in the Court of Subordinate Judge, (Now Joint District Judge). 3rd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the exparte decree. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.912 of 1993. From the record, it appears that two applications were filed for amendment of the application under Order IX, rule 13 which were allowed.

4. The case of the defendant was that it had neither any knowledge about the transfer of the suit from one Court to another nor its learned Advocate informed it about the transfer of the suit and as such, it could not appear when the suit was called on for hearing and decreed exparte. If the exparte decree was not set aside, the defendant would suffer irreparable loss and injury.

5. The miscellaneous case was contested by the plaintiff by filing written objection denying the material statements made in the application contending, inter alia, that the application was barred by limitation as the same was filed 1 (one) year and 6 (six) months after the suit was decreed exparte. The defendant intentionally allowed the suit to be decreed exparte, so it was not entitled to get the decree set aside.

6. The learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka by his order dated 13.04.1998 allowed the miscellaneous case, set aside the exparte decree and restored the suit to its file and number. Against the order of the learned Subordinate Judge, the plaintiff respondent filed Civil Revision No. 1998 of 1998 before the High Court Division and a learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the order passed the learned subordinate Judge.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 887 of 2002 and leave was granted giving rise to this appeal to consider the submission of the learned counsel as under:

"The learned Counsel for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division held that the Miscellaneous Case No. 912 of 1993 under Order 9 Rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed long after 30 days from the date of passing of the exparte decree dated 30.05.1992 and bench the same was barred by limitation, but failed to consider the vital aspect of the matter the Miscellaneous Case was filed within 30 days from the date of knowledge. He next submitted that from the judgment in the miscellaneous case it appears that The trial court took into consideration all the matters in which exparte decree was passed and held that the original suit was transferred from one court to another and the present petitioner was not informed of such transfer at different times and hence the petitioner was not aware of the exparte decree in question. The trial court further held that witness Nos. 2 and 3 for the petitioner in the Miscellaneous Case in their evidence categorically stated that they informed the petitioner about the exparte decree in question on 24.09.1993 and from that date Miscellaneous case so filed was well within time and as such the High Court Division was not justified in making the rule absolute."

8. Heard Mr. Mohammad Nazrul Islam, learned Counsel for the appellant who reiterated the submission on which leave was granted.

9. From the order of the learned Subordinate. Judge, it appears that he allowed the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code on the findings that after filing written statement the defendant suggested issues and thereafter the suit was transferred twice, i.e. to the Court of Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2 Dhaka and again to the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka where the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 306 of 1990. There was not the slightest proof that at any stage, after the suit was re-transferred to the Court (the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka) and before the exparte hearing, the defendant was aware about the transfer f the suit. Not only that, after the re-transfer of the suit date for peremptory hearing was fixed on o8.09.1999 directing the parties to get ready, but that order was not intimated or communicated to the defendant. The learned Subordinate Judge concluded that I the defendant was not aware about the transfer proceedings of the suit to the Court of Subordinate Judge, and commercial Court No. 2 and again re-transfer to the Court of the Subordinate Judge 3rd Court. Dhaka (in Bangla, the learned Subordinate Judge recorded his finding as ‘‘তারপর অত্রাদালত থেকে মামলাটি পুনরায় বদলী হয়ে সাব জজ ও বানিজ্যিক আদালত-০২ এ চলে যায় এবং নম্বর ২৫৭/৯০ অত:পর মামলাটি আবার আদরতে ফেরৎ আসে এবং মামলার নম্বর হয় ৩০৬/৯০ অত্র মামলাটি বানিজ্যিক আদালতে বদলী হয়ে যাওয়ায় এবং পুনরায় আদালতে আসায় এবং একতরফা শুনানী হওয়ায় কোনো পর্যায়েই মূল মামলার ৭ নং বিবাদী অর্থাৎ অত্র মিস কেসের দরখাস্তকারী জ্ঞাত ছিলেন এমন কোনো নূন্যতম নজির পাওয়া যায় না। এমনকি অত্রাদরতে মামলা বদলী হয়ে আসার পর ইং ০৮/০৯/৯৯ তারিখে চুড়ান্ত শুনানীর দিন ধার্য করার পর পক্ষগণকে প্রস্তুত থাকতে বলা হলেও উক্ত আদেশ ৭নং বিবাদীকে জ্ঞাত করা হয় নাই। অর্থাৎ অত্র মামলাটি বানিজ্যিক আদালতে বদরী হয়ে যাওয়ার এবং আবার ফেরৎ আসার কার্যক্রমে দরখাস্তকারী জ্ঞাত ছিরেন না।”

10. The learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 came to the further finding that the defendant could know about the exparte decree only on 24.09.1993; the defendant had no laches and because of non-communication of the fact of transfer of the suit twice in the same Court, which ought to , have been intimated to it, it was deprived of the chance to contest the suit and in order to secure ends of justice, the defendant should be given a chance to contest the suit by setting aside the exparte decree and accordingly allowed the miscellaneous case and set aside the exparte decree and restored the suit to its file and number.

11. The learned Judge of the Single Bench in setting aside the order of the learned Subordinate Judge did not at all advert his finding that after suggesting issue by defendant No. 7, the suit was transferred twice first to the Subordinate Judge, and commercial court No. 2, Dhaka from the court of subordinate Judge 3rd Court, Dhaka and then again was re-transferred to the said Court, i.e. the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka from the Court of Subordinate Judge and second Commercial Court, Dhaka, but the defendant was not at all intimated about the said fact of transfer. The learned Judge of the light Court Division only went by the fact that the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code was barred by limitation as the same was filed long after 30 days from the date of the exparte decree. The learned Judge approached the case absolutely mechanically and did not consider the pertinent board fact involved in the suit that the fact of transfer of the suit was not communicated to the defendant. In the context, the learned Judge also filed to consider rule 388(2) and note 1 thereto of the Civil Rules and Order which has mandated that the fact of transfer of a case from one Court to another Court on an off date must be communicated either to the party concerned or to his advocate (see the case of M.A. Wahab and another-Vs-Abul Kalam and another 44 DLR(AD) 13.)

<u>12. It needs to be mentioned that though the plaintiff-opposite party (in the miscellaneous case) filed written objection, he did not examine any witness and this failed to produce any evidence that the order of transfer of the suit was either communicated to the defendant or to its lawyer and that the order fixing the date of peremptory hearing of the suit was shown to the learned Advocate of the defendant as found by the learned Subordinate Judge.</u>

<u>13. It is true that the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code was filed after 30 (thirty) days from the date of the decree, but sufficient explanations were given for filing the same out of time and prayer was made for condoning the delay. But the learned Judge considered nothing. The learned Judge did not also advert the findings and the reasoning of the Subordinate Judge in condoning the delay in filing the application out of time. The only reason assigned by the learned Judge in making the Rule absolute was that the application was filed beyond 30 (days). In the context, the learned Judge failed to consider that section 5 of the limitation was applicable to an application filed under IX, rule 13 of the Code beyond limitation and thus erred in law in interfering with the order of the learned Subordinate Judge.</u>

<u>14. For the discussions made hereinbefore, we merit in the appeal.</u>

15. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and order is set aside and those of the trial court is restored.

16. No order as to cost.

End.

caseno: Civil Revision No. 2170 of 2006
lawyer:
Mr. S.A. M. Mahbub Elahi with Mr. Zahurul Alam, Advocates ------For the petitioners 
Mr. Md. Abdus Samad Kamal, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Sabruddin @ Shafiuddin and others ------ Defendant Nos. 21-23 Appellant-Petitioners
Vs
Kafiluddin Dewan and 4 others ------ Plaintiff-Respondent -Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker,  J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj, in Title Appeal No.91 of 2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 173 of 2002 should not be set aside and/or pass such other order or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite party Nos. 1-5 being plaintiffs filed the original Title Suit being No. 173 of 2002 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, District-Manikganj against the defendant-petitioners praying for partition of the land described in the schedule and also for a declaration of title and recovery of possession with a further declaration that the S.A. and R.S. Khatian in respect of the land described in the schedule Nos.' and 2 of the plaint are illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia, that the land described in schedule no.1 of the plaint belonged to one Babor Ali and his brother Buchai Sheikh. The land of schedule Nos. 2 and 3 was recorded in the name of Buchai Sheikh. Babor Ali died before publication of D.S. record leaving behind his wife Tamasha Bewa. Buchai Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Meher Jan Bewa. The land described in schedule 1 was recorded in the name of Meherjan Bewa and Tamasha Bewa correctly. Tamasha Bewa and Meherjan Bewa granted korfa pattan of the land described in schedule nos. 1 and 2 in favour of one Saber Dewan and his wife Firoza Begum on 8th Srabon, 1328 B.S. Tamasha Bewa gave korfa pattan of the land described in schedule-3 in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum on 14th Aswin, 1329 B.S. Thereafter, getting the land by way of korfa pattan the pattan holders Saber Dewan and Feroza possessed the same described in schedule nos. 1-3. Saber Dewan died leaving behind his wife Feroza Begum, two sons Karim and Moksed and one daughter Hatunnessa. During the life time of Saber Dewan his one son Md. Ashraf Ali died leaving behind daughter Ayatunnessa and Ayatunnessa died leaving behind the plaintiffs as her heirs. The S.A. record was prepared in the name of Ayatunnessa and thus the plaintiffs after acquiring the suit land measuring 1.25 acres by way of inheritance and purchase sold 07 (seven) decimals of land in favour of the defendant No.2 and the rest land measuring I. I8 acres are being possessed by them with the defendants in ejmali. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the land of schedule-I of the plaint has been wrongly recorded in the names of the predecessor of the defendant nos. 21-23. Prior to the filing of the original suit the plaintiff nos. 1-4 along with others filed a Title Suit being No. 132 of 1994 in the court of Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj, which was renumbered as Title Suit No. 94 of 2000. The suit was dismissed and against that order of dismissal the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 18 of 2001 which was also dismissed and the learned appellate court vide his judgment and decree dated. 13.06.2002 observed that the plaintiffs may prefer partition suit in a competent court of law. Therefore, the plaintiffs filed the original suit. 
3. The contrary case of the contesting defendants is such that the suit as it was framed is not maintainable and there is no cause of action. The suit is bad for defect of the parties and hotchpotch defect. The further case of the defendants to that suit is such that the plaintiffs have no right, title interest and possession in the disputed land and the suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata. The disputed 2.56 acres of land belonged to Babor Ali and Buchai Sheikh. The D.S. record was prepared in their names but in the dakhalker column of the D.S. record the names of one Tamasha Bewa and Meherjan Bewa were inserted, who are the wives of Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh. The share of Tamasha was transferred to Meherjan and Meherjan become the owner of entire 2.56 acres of land. The positive case of the defendants is such that during the life time of Tamasha Bewa and Meheijan they never gave any korfa pattan in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum. Saber Dewan along with his wife Feroza Begum were in fact not the owners of the land described in the schedule of the plaint by virtue of korfa pattan. The R.S. Khatian no. 199 of Mouza Kashimnagar and R.S. Khatian No. 226 of Mouza Barabaka were recorded in the name of Shamsuddin alone which was correct. Shamsuddin owned and possessed 1.28 acres of land and constructed huts therein. He also planted various trees there and that he was not the permissive possessor in the land described in the schedule of plaint. Shamsuddin died leaving behind one son the defendant no. 21 and two daughters the defendant nos. 22 and 23. The further case of the defendants is such that the plaintiffs to this suit filed a Title Suit being No. 132 of 1999 which was renumbered as 94 of 2000. That suit was dismissed on contest. Against that judgment and decree plaintiffs preferred a Title Appeal being No. 18 of 2001 and that appeal was also dismissed on contest. The statements made by the plaintiffs with regard to their alleged title are totally contrary to the statement made by them in their previous Title Suit No. 132 of 1999. 
4. The learned trial court after examining the witnesses from the sides of the respective parties decreed the suit in the preliminary form by his judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005. Being aggrieved the present defendant-petitioners preferred a title appeal in the court of learned District Judge. Manikganj being Title Appeal No. 91 of 2005 which was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj and the leaned lower appellate court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 disallowed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 
5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree the defendant-appellant-petitioners have preferred this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of stay. 
6. Mr. S.A.M. Mahbuh Elahi, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioners while Mr. Md. Abdus Samad Kamal, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 
7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that both the courts below during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity and without considering the material evidence on record they committed error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the lower appellate court without discussing and considering the evidence of the witnesses decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiffs on surmise and conjecture and without discussions upon the issues framed upheld the findings of the trial court which is violative of the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Both the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiffs are claiming title and partition on the basis of kabla deeds marked as exhibit-3 series and same private documents of koda pattan exhibits-2, 2(ka). Having failed to prove these documents under sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act and in absence of proof of its execution the documents does not create any presumption of its genuineness and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate also submits that the courts below were totally failed to assess the material exhibits of the defendants marked as Exhibits-`Ka' and gala' series. They also failed to evaluate Exhibit-'1Ca' properly. The learned lower appellate court acted illegally in affirming the decree of the trial court ignoring the oral and documentary evidence of the defendants by resorting to hypothetical assumption and both the courts below erred in law in not considering the respective cases of the parties in jaxta position with same yardstick weightment and rejected the defendant's case as regard title without proper application of judicial mind and the same has caused miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that in the impugned judgment and decree there has been apparent misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and as such the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be interfered with. 
8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal committed no illegality or irregularity. As regard the basis of the plaintiff-opposite parties case in respect of the disputed property on korfa pattan, the koda pattan papers has already been marked exhibits after formal proof according to law and at this stage the defendants are stopped from challenging the said basis of claim of the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate. further submits that in the original suit the plaintiffs prayed for three separate relief but the court below granted only one relief in favour of the plaintiffs without debarring the plaintiff from getting subsequent relief which were sought for by the plaintiff-opposite parties. No relief was granted on the prayer for recovery of khash possession in respect of 17 decimals of land in which admittedly the plaintiffs are ousted from their possession by the defendants illegally. Furthermore; no relief was given by the courts below on the prayer of declaration that the khatian in respect of 49 decimals of land is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs. Apart from this; the trial court as well as the appellate court during disposal of the original suit and its appeal failed to consider that the plaintiffs to the suit. who are the present opposite parties prayed for separate saham in respect of 1.18 acres of land. The trial court without assigning any reason only gave 1.02 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs and there is no explanation on the remaining 16 decimals of land. Beside this no courts during their judgment and findings gave any observation on the plaintiff's specific contention of giving oral permission to the defendants to posses 17 decimals of land in the disputed holding and as a result the plaintiffs are not also happy with the judgments.

9. Heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the case records, exhibited papers, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected papers. 

10. It appears from the case record that the plaintiffs to the suit in their pleading asserts that the land described in schedule 1 of the plaint originally belonged to Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh and the land of schedule nos. 2 and 3 were recorded in the D.S. khatian which stands recorded in the name of Buchai Sheikh only. It was further contended that Babar Ali died before the publication of D.S. record leaving behind his wife Tamasha Bibi. Buchai Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Meherjan and in this way after the death of Babar Ali and Buchai Sheikh their wives by way of inheritance acquired the land in dispute. The land described in schedule nos. 1 and 2 of the plaint was recorded in the names of Meherunnessa and Tamasha Bewa and the land described in schedule 3 was recorded in the name of Tamasha Bewa only. The basis of claim from the side of the plaintiffs in respect of their schedule property is koda pattan in the year 1328 and in the year 1329 respectively. Their specific contention as it appears is such that the land of schedule Nos. 1 and 2 were transferred by Tamasha and Meherjan in favour of Saber Dewan and his wife Feroza Begum on 8th Srabon, 1328 B.S. Subsequently Tamasha Bewa on 14th Aswin of 1329 B.S. transferred the land of schedule no.3 in favour of Saber Dewan and Feroza Begum by way of korfa pattan at a salami of Taka 100/-. The said korfa pattan has been categorically challenged from the side of the contesting defendants and in this context it is the specific assertion of the defendant-appellant-petitioners that the basis of claim of the plaintiffs, i.e. the korfa settlement in the name of their predecessor in interest not at all proved under the purview of sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act. In this regard sections 67 and 68 of the Evidence Act contemplates that the documents alleged to have been executed by a person after putting signature or left thumb impression is required to be proved wholly or partly by the person, who is directly involved in its execution. Mere production of the documents is not at all sufficient for proof. The proof would be in compliance of provisions and the aforesaid sections. Therefore, a document which is not proved as required by this section; is inadmissible in evidence. 

11. On careful scrutiny over the impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below it is obvious to note that both the courts below have hopelessly failed to appreciate the actual position of law in taking cognizance of the document produced which is the basis of claim of the plaintiffs. Furthermore, apparently the impugned judgment and decree is not passed in compliance of the provisions laid down in Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and it is also apparent from the face of the Records that the trial court during disposal of the original suit failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of law as provided in Order XX, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure in stating decision on each issue. Gross illegality was done during disposal of the original suit and its subsequent appeal and it is an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Apart from this; in view of the argument advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the opposite parties in consultation with the original case record I have every reason to appreciate the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties and it is most unfortunate that the trial court as well as the appellate court without going into the merit of the suit and materials on record including the prayer portion of the plaint in a evasive manner disposed of the suit and its subsequent appeal which is arbitrary and not desirable. There is no explanation even from the side of the trial court as to why the relief which were sought for was not granted or refused. There is no findings in respect of the quantum of land for which the share allegedly was given in favour of the plaintiffs out of the total land. Despite 16 decimals of land has been left out the reason for which that portion of land was not given not at all cited within the four corners of the findings and decision. During arguments the learned counsel on behalf of the defendant-petitioners referred a decision of this court reported in 43 DLR 221 which is most appropriate here and have got every nexus in the instant case. In the case of Dewan Mohammad Safare Ali & others —vs.-People's Republic of Bangladesh, reported in 43 DLR(1991)221 it was held that the object of rule 31 of Or. XLI of the Code of Civil Procedure is such that the Appellate Court must consider independently the relevant salient points which arose for adjudication and to discuss evidence led by the parties as well as point of law. In the instant case the Appellate Court obviously did not discuss each issue separately nor gave any independent findings on each issue after proper assessment and preponderance of evidence and thereby the impugned judgment and decree suffers from patent illegality and material irregularity which was violative of the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Our Apex Court in the case of Hajarilal Mondal and others —vs.- Md. Mozajfor Bepari and others, reported in 8 BLC (AD) 77 held that "it is a settled principle of law that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will discuss and reassess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the finding of the trial Court." 

12. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that both the courts below during disposal of the suit and subsequent appeal committed gross error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and without applying judicial mind in a hasty manner the courts decided the issues without proper assessment of the evidence and appreciation of law. Hence, I have every reason to draw such inference that both the judgments and decree are not a judgment in accordance with law and in such a case the decree should be set aside and the case is remanded for disposal under the findings and observations made in the body of the judgment. 

13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15.02.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Manikganj, in Title Appeal No. 91 of 2005 and the judgment and decree dated 25.04.2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 173 of 2002 are hereby set aside. 

14. The order of stay granted earlier by this court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. The original suit be send back on remand for fresh trial within 02(two) months from the date of receipt of the Records. 

15. Communicate the judgment and order and send down the lower Court's record at once.

End.
