Mr. A.N.M. Bashir Ullah J:- This Rule on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the CPC) at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner was issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 04.04.2006 (decree signed on 12.04.2006) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Natore in Title Appeal no. 178 of 1998 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment dated 12.07.1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Gurudaspur, Natore in Other Class Suit no.35 of 1987 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the opposite party no.10 Mrs. Ayesha Khatun Bibi instituted Other Class Suit no. 468 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, Natore for partition of the suit land seeking a saham for 1.88 acres of land with a further declaration that the partition deed being no. 20913) dated 21.04.1975 of Rajshahi Sadar Sub-Registrar Office is collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon her contending inter-alia that 6.88 acres of land appertaining to C.S khatian no. no. 102 corresponding to S.A khatian no. 240 and R.S. Khatian 467 originally belonged to Jitu Prang who had two sons Pachan and Soleman. During the life time of Jitu Prang, his son Pachan died leaving daughter Ayesha Khatun Bibi. Jitu Prang died on 25e February, 1962 leaving son Soleman and daughter of pre-deceased son Pachan. In view of the provisions of Muslim Family Law Ordinance, 1961 Soleman and Ayesha Khatun Bibi had inherited equal share in the properties left by their predecessor Jitu Prang. 

3. Jitu Prang though died on 25th February, 1962 but Soleman in order to deprive 
Ayesha Khatun Bibi from her clue share in the properties left by Jitu Prang tried to establish that Jitu Prang died on 25th February, 1961. Ayesha Khatun sold. 69 acres of land to Nur Mohammad Sarker, the defendant no. 7. Soleman died leaving behind the defendant nos. 1-6 as his heirs. The defendants in order to deprive Ayesha Khatun had created a partition deed dated 20.05.1975 but Ayesha had no knowledge about the said deed. She came to know on 27.07.1971 about it and on going to the said deed she found that she had been deprived from her due share. Ayesha Khatun Bibi has 1.88 acres of land into the partible land but the defendants denied to partition the suit land amicably giving the due share to Ayesha Khatun Bibi, hence the suit. 

4. After filing of the suit there appears a decree on compromise against the defendant nos. 1-9 by the judgment and order dated 12.06.1978. The record further shows that. Ayesha Khatun Bihi flied Title Suit no. 621 of 1978 for cancellation of the aforesaid compromise decree dated 12.06.1978 alleging some fraud on her in order to obtain the exparte decree and the said title Suit no. 621 of 1978 was decreed by its judgment and order dated 15.05.1984 setting aside the decree passed on 12.06.1978 on the basis of solenama and concomitantly the Title suit no. 468 of 1977 was restored and was re-numbered as Title Suit no. 35 of 1987 on 23.03.1987. 

5. The defendant nos. 1-6 filing written statement contested in the suit. The case of the defendants are that the suit is not maintainable in its present from and the suit is bad for non-joinder of parties etcetera. The further case of the defendants are that Jitu Prang being the owner and the possessor of the partible land had died leaving only son Soleman, the predecessor of defendant nos. 1-6. Pachan, the another son of Jitu Prang died on 20.02.1961 as such, Ayesha Khatun Bibi, the daughter of pre-deceased son of Jitu Prang did not inherit any land as heirs of Jitu Prang in to the partible land. Although Ayesha Khatun Bibi did not inherit any land into the property of her grandfather Jitu Prang but to serve the interest of humanity and mankind she was given some land amicably through the disputed deed of partition. But Ayesha Khatun Bibi could not be satisfied of the said portion rather she becoming greedy for more land filed the false suit which is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

6. The defendant no. 7 filed a separate written statement in the trial Court describing a case which appears to be similar with the case of the plaintiff that during the life time of Jitu Prang his son Pachan died leaving the daughter Ayesha Khatun Bibi and after the death of Jitu Prang his son Soleman and predeceased sons daughter Ayesha Khatun Bibi got the land in equal share left by Jitu Prang. The defendant no.7 purchased .65 acres of land from Ayesha Khatun Bibi and he has been possessing the same. 

7. On-06.07.1987 plaintiff Ayesha Bibi filed a petition for withdrawal of the suit. The trial Court with some remarks allowed the said petition subject to deposit of Taka 3,000/- as costs within 23.7.1987. But the record does not show any such deposit on behalf of Ayesah Khatun Bibi as a result the conditional order of withdrawal of the suit at the instance of Ayesha Khatun Bibi was not affected. On 16.11.1988 on a prayer of defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker he was transposed as plaintiff in to the suit and the record further shows that on an application filed by the added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant no.7 by the order of the Court dated 22.06.1997. 

8. At trial, the trial Court framed as many as 5 issues to dispose of the suit. The plaintiff examined 6 witnesses while the defendants examined 5 witnesses and both the parties filed some documentary evidences which were marked as exhibits. The trial Court by its judgment dated 12.07. I 998 dismissed the suit. The plaintiff against the said judgment preferred Title Appeal no. 178 of 1998 in the Court of District Judge. Nature which has 'been heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Natore who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 4.4.2006 dismissed the appeal affirming those of the judgment of the trial Court. The plaintiff-petitioner being. aggrieved by dissatisfied with the said judgment of the appellate Court below moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. A.K.M. Shamsuddin, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner supports the Rule. He submits that both the Courts below should have found that the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant and the original defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker has been transposed as plaintiff in the suit and there was no inconsistency in the case of former plaintiff and the defendant no.7 and infect after such transposition the plaint was not amended to bring the actual case of Nur Mohammad Sarker in the plaint but same happened for the laches of the conducting lawyer of the petitioner and for the said technical defects both the Courts  below dismissed the suit as well as the appeal. 


10. He categorically submits that Ayesha Khatun Bibi in his plaint admitted that she had sold .69 acres of land to Nur Mohammad Sarker (initially the defendant no.7 later on has become the plaintiff) and in fact Nur Mohammad Sarker to protect his interest into the said land was transposed as plaintiff but inadvertently no amendment was sought for in the plaint as a result Nur Mohammad Sarker was deprived from his desired relief. He also submits that the trial Court on the wrong assessment of the evidence and other materials on record came to a wrong conclusion that Jitu Prang died in 1961. He lastly submits that if the suit is sent back on remand that will be a proper justice to the present petitioner Nur Mohammad Sarker and in that case he will get a proper chance to amend the plaint seeking his proper relief, so, the Rule should be made absolute setting aside the judgments of the Courts below. 
11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner in alternatively also submits that though issue no. 4 to the effect as to whether plaintiff (Nur Mohammad Sarker) has the right, title and interest into the suit land was framed in the suit, but the same was not decided on merit as the case of plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker did not find place in the plaint. So, for any reason if the Rule is discharged, the plaintiff-petitioner may be given a chance for filing a suit afresh to protect his interest into the suit land. 
12. On the other hand. Mr. Md. Alamgir Mostafizur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 opposing the Rule submits that the plaintiff Ahesha Khatun Bibi claiming some share in the partible land filed the suit in the year 1977 and though immediately after filing of the suit in the year 1978 the suit was decreed on compromise against the defendant. but for the reasons best known to Ayesha Khatun Bibi challenging the said decree dated 12.06.1978 filed an independent suit being no. 621 of 1978 and the said suit was decreed exparte on 15.05.1984. There after the original Title Suit being no. 621 of 1978 was restored in its original file and number but at that stage it was re-numbered as title Suit no.35 of 1987. 
13. He further submits that the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi by that time was convinced that she had no good case as such she filed a petition for withdrawal of the suit and the same was allowed on 06.07.1987. But since she failed to fulfill the condition of depositing Taka 3,000/- in the Court as costs within 23.07 .1987 as such the-order dated 06.7.1987 was not effected at all and thereafter the defendant no.7 Nur Mohammad Sarker was transposed as plaintiff on 16.11.1988 and almost alter 9 years on 22.06.1997 the original plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi was transposed as defendant. 

14. He further submits that the suit was dismissed on contest after almost 10 years from the date of transposition of No Mohammad Sarker as plaintiff on 12.07.1998 but with in this long 10 years the new plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker did not feel any necessity to amend the plaint to brine his exact case in the scene. He also submits that on this ground the suit was dismissed by the trial Court and when the appeal was filed in 1998 the same was decided by the appellate Court below almost after 8 years of its filing in 1996 and with in this long 8 years the plaintiff did not file any petition seeking the relief which has been sought in this Rule. The new plaintiff after pronouncing the judgment by the trial Court got the message as to the reason of the dismissal judgment but even then the plaintiff petitioner did not take proper step in the appellate Court below. The plaintiff-petitioner with an intention to cause harm to the defendant-opposite parties has been continuing with the suit. Had the plaintiff-petitioner any good intention to have a proper adjudication on the matter he could have sought the amendment at the appellate stage also but during the pendency of the appeal for long 8N cars he did not take any step. So, alter 36 years of the suit, a suit like this should not be sent back on remand causing serious mischief to the defendant-opposite parties. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 
15.1 have considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

16. On going to the materials on record it appears that the suit has a very chequered history during its long pendency. The suit was started in the year 1977 and immediately after filing of the suit it was decreed on compromise on the basis of a solenama. Subsequently, the same was challenged by the plaintiff Ayesha Khatun Bibi and the decree on compromise was set aside and the original suit was restored and re-numbered as Title Suit no. 35 of 1987. Thereafter, the present plaintiff was transposed as plaintiff from his earlier position of defendant no. 7 on 16.1 1.1988 and after 10 years of his such transposition the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on contest by its judgment dated 12.07.1998. 

17. The trial Court though did not decide the title of the plaintiff but came to a conclusion that Jitu Prang died on 20.01.1961. The trial Court also observed that though Nur Mohammad Sarker became the plaintiff but there appears no case of Nur Mohammad Sarker in the plaint and ultimately the suit was dismissed by the trial Court on that count. 

18. The appeal was pending for 8 years and ultimately the judgment of the trial Court was affirmed in the appeal. In the case of Abdul Kader-vs-Noor Mohammad 36 DLR(AD) 261 it was held by our Apex Court that the findings on the basis of no evidence is of no legal consequence and the findings of the Court below could he disturbed if there is any misreading of evidence or misconstruction of the evidence. In the case of 18 BLD(AD) 15 it was also held that a revisional Court also may consider the evidence which was not considered by the lower appellate Court below. In the case of Abdul Gam-vs-N/1d. Abdur Razzak 62 DLR(AD) 242 it was held by our Apex Court that a revisional Court cannot reverse the concurrent findings of the Courts below based on proper appreciation of the evidence. 

19. Thus the preponderant views emerged from the above authorities that the concurrent findings of the fact of the Courts below cannot be disturbed if the same is based on the proper appreciation of legal evidence but the concurrent findings can be disturbed if the same is not based on the proper assessment of the evidence on record. 

20. On going to the judgment of the trial Court I find that the trial Court very meticulously scanned and considered the evidence on record in respect of the death of Jitu Prang and thereafter came to a conclusion that he died in the year 1961. There appears no misreading or non-reading or non-consideration of the evidence in respect of the death of Jitu Prang. The learned Advocate of the petitioner could not show the misreading on non reading or non consideration of the evidence on record in respect of the death of Jitu Prang. So, I find it difficult to differ with the concurrent findings of the Courts below in respect of the death of Jitu Prang. 

21. As I have found in this Rule that the learned Advocate for the petitioner frankly submits that after the transposition of the defendant no.7 as plaintiff he should have amended the plaint seeking his accurate relief but that has not been done for the mistake of his engaged lawyer. It is fact that after the transposition of Nur Mohammad Sarker as plaintiff from the category of the defendant the suit continued in the trial Court for 10 years in the earlier form. If it is conceded for a moment that inadvertently or for any other reason the plaint could not be amended seeking the proper relief for Nur Mohammad Sarker but what will be the excuse during the pendency of the appeal in the appellate Court below as because the trial Court in its judgment pointed out very categorically the lacking of amendment in the plaint in the following manner: ‘‘ মূল মামলার ৭ নং বিবাদী বাদী হইয়া বাদীনিকে বিবাদী করিয়া অত্র মামলাটি চালাইতেছেন। অথচ ৭নং বিবাদী বাদী শ্রেণীভূক্ত হইয়া কোন বক্তব্য বলেন নাই বা বাদীর মামলার আরজীতে সমর্থন করিয়া কোন দরখাস্ত দায়ের করেন নাই" 

22. From the findings of the trial Court it appears that he had visualised the necessity of the amendment of the plaint for the proper remedy to the transposed plaintiff. It is very surprising to me that even after that sharp findings of the trial Court no proper step was taken after filing of the appeal to address the lacuna of the plaintiff as observed in the judgment of the trial Court, though the appeal was pending for the last 8 years and within this long period the plaintiff- appellant again remained mum and at this stage after a total span of 36 years of filing of the suit he has been seeking a remand order from this Court giving him a chance to amend the plaint appears to be unjust and unwarranted. 

23. In the case of 20 BLD(AD) 105 it was held by our Apex Court that it is now a settled principle of law that a suit should not be remanded to give any party an opportunity to fill up any lacuna by bringing further amendment or by adducing further evidence. The same view also endorsed in neumorous cases including 51 DLR 289 wherein it was held by this Court that where a party had the opportunity to adduce all necessary evidence in the trial Court but did not, in such a case the suit should he remanded to adduce fresh evidence. 

24. In my consideration if it is conceded for a moment that when the suit was pending in the trial Court the plaintiff' could not understand the necessity of the amendment of the plaint but whenever the suit was dismissed by the trial Court for want or his case in the plaint he did not amend the plaint seeking his real remedy at the appellate stage although the appellant had the opportunity to seek proper remedy there what has been praying now before me.

25. Since the plaintiff had the opportunity to seek the amendment of the plaint and to adduce the evidence at the appeal but he did not avail the same. So, after a long gap of 36 years I find that the suit should not be sent back on remand causing irreparable mischief and harm to the opposite parties. Thus, I find no illegality or error of law in the judgment of the Courts below and as such I fail to point out any merit in the Rule. 

26. From the materials on record it appears that it is fact that the case of the added plaintiff was never considered either by the trial Court or by the appellate Court below as because his case was not brought into the plaint. The plaint was filed by Ayesha Khatun Bibi to protect her interest though the added plaintiff had purchased .69 acres of land from the said Ayesha Khatun Bibi. But in fact the specific case of added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker was not considered by the Courts below as the same was not available in the plaint although issue was framed to that effect as to the whether the plaintiff has right, title and interest into the suit land. So, in view of the facts and circumstances of the case though the Rule is going to be discharged but the plaintiff-petitioner may be allowed to file a suit afresh to protect his interest into his purchased land subject to protecting the findings and decisions of the Courts below as to the death or Jitu Prang in the year 1961. If any suit is filed by the added plaintiff Nur Mohammad Sarker to protect his interest for his purchased land the issue as to the death of Jitu Prang as has been settled cannot be opened again. 

27. In. the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. 

28. Let a copy of this Judgment and order along with the lower Courts record be sent to the Court concerned. 
End.
